title: Treasury International Capital Data for August 2026
body: October 16, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for August 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for September 2026, is scheduled for November 18, 2026. The sum total in August of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $199.8 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $178.5 billion, and net foreign official inflows were $21.3 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in August; their net purchases were $300.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $257.8 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $42.9 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $21.6 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $279.2 billion in August. Foreign residents decreased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $47.8 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $37.8 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents decreased by $41.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries. title: We’re sharing 3 tips to study smarter with Gemini Notebook.
body: We’re sharing 3 tips to study smarter with Gemini Notebook. Lisa Oguike Education team Oct 16, 2026 Studying for exams can feel overwhelming. To help you prepare, we recently launched three new features in Gemini Notebook to make your learning more structured and engaging. Short Video Overviews : If you’re trying to quickly grasp a tricky concept, you can now generate a 60-second Short Video Overview to help you unpack it. They’re easy to watch on-the-go or share with a classmate. Interactive Learning Overviews : If you have dozens of notes, lectures, and readings to review, you can create an Interactive Learning Overview under Reports to walk you through your material, step by step. It weaves together summaries and studio outputs like slides, quizzes, and flashcards, all grounded strictly in your coursework. Expanded quiz formats : We also added more ways for you to test your knowledge with new quiz formats, including short-answer, multi-select, and fill-in-the blank options. After testing yourself or reviewing your flashcards, you can ask your notebook for feedback to pinpoint where you should focus next. Try them with your own materials at notebook.google .

title: The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Tennessee Joins DOJ Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing Tax Fraud
body: Press Release The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Tennessee Joins DOJ Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing Tax Fraud Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Tennessee More than 30 U.S. Attorney’s Offices joined the Fraud Division in bringing enforcement actions against alleged fraudsters NASHVILLE – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Tennessee announced charges as part of nationwide enforcement actions led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Tennessee was a key participant in this surge effort. Between early September and today, federal prosecutors across the country facilitated fraud enforcement actions spanning over 76 criminal defendants reaching more than $490,000,000 in intended loss to American taxpayers . According to court records, Thomas William Jones, 59 years old, of Brentwood, Tennessee, pleaded guilty last month to one count of failing to collect and pay taxes to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), announced United States Attorney for the Middle District of Tennessee Braden H. Boucek. Jones was the owner and operator of Alternative Solutions Consulting Corporation (“ASCC”), a software consulting company in Franklin, Tennessee, where he employed others and maintained the ASCC’s finances. Jones controlled ASCC’s bank account and paid his employees from this account. As an employer, Jones had a duty to truthfully account for and pay the required federal income and employment taxes. Between 2014 and 2023, Jones failed to file the appropriate forms with the IRS for ASCC to report his employees’ wages. Jones also did not make payments to the IRS for federal income and Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) tax withholdings which were required to be taken from his employees’ paychecks. In addition, Jones did not make payments to the IRS for the matching portion of the FICA taxes ( i.e ., the employer contributions to Social Security and Medicare) that he was required to make. The total amount of taxes Jones failed to collect and pay is not more than $1,975,964.24. Jones was charged by an Information on July 7, 2026. He pled guilty on September 1, 2026. He faces up to five years in federal prison. U.S. District Court Judge Eli J. Richardson scheduled Jones’s sentencing for January 15, 2027. *** On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The IRS and the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI) investigated the case. Criminal Chief Ahmed A. Safeeullah is prosecuting the case. ###### Contact Steve Stanley Public Affairs Officer Steve.Stanley2@usdoj.gov (615) 401-6615 Updated October 16, 2026 Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Tennessee, Middle

title: Federal Jury Finds Minnetonka Man Guilty on All Counts for Threatening to Murder Federal Judges and Elected Officials
body: Press Release Federal Jury Finds Minnetonka Man Guilty on All Counts for Threatening to Murder Federal Judges and Elected Officials Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Minnesota MINNEAPOLIS – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that Jeffrey Allen Petersen, 68, of Minnetonka, Minnesota, was found guilty on 10 counts of threatening to murder U.S. judges and elected officials, and 10 counts of interstate transmission of threats to injure. A federal jury found Petersen guilty of all 20 counts on October 15, 2026, after a trial before U.S. District Judge Patrick J. Schiltz. A sentencing hearing will be scheduled by the Court at a date yet to be determined. “My office has no tolerance for political violence and threats of political violence,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen. “We will prosecute—to the fullest extent of the law—those who intimidate or threaten public servants who are just doing their jobs.” “Threats against federal judges and lawmakers strike at the heart of our judicial system and our democracy,” said FBI Minneapolis Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson. “The FBI Minneapolis Joint Terrorism Task Force will investigate and disrupt individuals who attempt to intimidate or harm public officials. At a time when Minnesota communities are especially mindful of political violence, this conviction on all 20 counts reflects the strength of our partnerships and our unwavering commitment to protecting those who serve the public.” According to court documents and evidence introduced at trial, in July 2025, the U.S. Marshals Service for the District of Maryland received a report from their judicial security intelligence unit regarding threatening comments posted to an article on a website referencing a federal judge in that District. On at least one website, Petersen used the username, “Adam Lanza,” the mass murderer who shot and killed 26 people, 20 of whom were school children between the ages of six and seven years old, at Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012. Image 1: Online post from Petersen Image 2: Online post from Petersen The U.S. Marshals Service investigated the post and found it was made with an IP address assigned to Petersen with a service address in Minnetonka, Minnesota. The U.S. Marshals Service then referred the matter to the FBI. During the investigation, law enforcement received additional reports concerning similar threatening comments posted on other sites toward federal judges and various elected officials throughout the United States. The username of some of the posts was “Behring.a,” and the full registered account name was, “Anders Breivik Behring.” Breivik is the name of the mass murderer who shot and killed 77 people in 2011 at a summer camp in Norway in “support of white supremacy.” The username for some of the other posts was “james holmes,” the 2012 Aurora Colorado theater mass murderer who killed 12 people and injured 62 others during a mass shooting event. The investigation revealed that the IP address of these usernames also traced back to Petersen in Minnesota. Image 3: Online post from Petersen Image 4: Online post from Petersen After learning that Petersen was the registered user for the accounts making the threatening posts on various platforms, federal law enforcement agents obtained and executed a federal search warrant at Petersen’s Minnetonka residence and recovered several electronic devices, which were later forensically examined. The forensic examinations showed that Petersen used the associated email addresses that were used to make the threatening posts on various online platforms. Law enforcement additionally found a June 2025 web search history on one of Petersen’s devices with terms including, “MN senators shot,” “adam lanza,” “anders brevik,” and “james holmes.” In total, Petersen’s posts threatened to murder eight federal judges, including an Associate Supreme Court Justice, and at least four elected United States Officials. This case was the result of an investigation by the U.S. Marshals Service and the FBI, with assistance from other federal and local law enforcement partners. Assistant United States Attorneys Albania Concepcion, Michael Blackburn, and Benjamin Bejar are prosecuting this case. Contact usamn.pressoffice@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Domestic Terrorism Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Minnesota

title: Foreign National Pleads Guilty to Illegally Obtaining U.S. Citizenship and U.S. Passport
body: Press Release Foreign National Pleads Guilty to Illegally Obtaining U.S. Citizenship and U.S. Passport Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey NEWARK, N.J. – A foreign national and convicted felon pleaded guilty to unlawful procurement of naturalization and passport fraud, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Miguel Dario Bautista Jimenez, a/k/a “Carlos Chapman Hernandez,” a/k/a “Carlos Hernandez,” 42, of Hoboken, New Jersey pleaded guilty to a two-count Indictment charging him with unlawful procurement of naturalization, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 1425(b) and 2, and passport fraud, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 1542 and 2, on October 14, 2026 before U.S. District Judge Stanley R. Chesler in Newark federal court. According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: Miguel Dario Bautista Jimenez, a citizen of the Dominican Republic, was removed from the United States in or around 2013, following a criminal conviction in New York for an aggravated felony.  In or around June 2014, Bautista re-entered the United States using a false identity.  Bautista applied for legal permanent residence and naturalization falsely stating that his name was “Carlos Chapman Hernandez,” a person born in Cuba, and falsely stating that he had never been convicted of a crime, had never been removed from the United States, and had never been to prison.  Bautista used the false identity to fraudulently obtain U.S. citizenship documents through naturalization, including a U.S. passport. The charges of unlawful procurement of naturalization and passport fraud each carry a maximum penalty of ten years’ imprisonment.  Each offense carries a maximum fine of $250,000, or twice the gross loss or gain from the offense, whichever is greatest. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of Homeland Security Investigations in Newark, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy, the Social Security Administration, Office of the Inspector General, New York Field Division, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Amy Connelly, the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service, New York Field Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Nicholas Fanelli, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, with the investigation leading to the guilty plea. The government is represented by Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Priscilla Gabela and Assistant U.S. Attorney Katherine M. Romano of the Criminal Division in Newark. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. ### Defense counsel: Carlos Diaz-Cobo, Esq. bautista.indictment.pdf Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Fraud Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-223
retained_feed_body: A foreign national and convicted felon pleaded guilty to unlawful procurement of naturalization and passport fraud.

title: Missouri Sex Offender Admits Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material
body: Press Release Missouri Sex Offender Admits Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri ST. LOUIS – A registered sex offender on Friday admitted viewing child sexual abuse material that he found online. Corey Adam Oliver, 53, pleaded guilty Friday in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to one count of possession of child pornography. In December of 2024, a Cyber Tipline report to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children indicated that Oliver had uploaded child sexual abuse material (CSAM) to Bing’s image search application. On January 14, 2025, the Missouri State Highway Patrol obtained a search warrant for Oliver’s home near Bismarck, in St. Francois County. In an interview with law enforcement, Oliver initially denied viewing or receiving CSAM. After he failed a consensual polygraph examination, he admitted using a tablet to do so. Oliver was required to register as a sex offender after having been convicted in Louisiana in 2000 of the felony offenses of molestation of a juvenile and carnal knowledge of a juvenile and in Georgia in 2007 of the felony offenses of enticing a child for indecent purposes and interference with child custody. Oliver is scheduled to be sentenced in January. The U.S. Attorney’s office will recommend 15 years in prison, followed by a lifetime on supervised release. The Missouri State Highway Patrol investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jillian Anderson prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Department of Justice Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . Contact Robert Patrick, Public Affairs Officer, robert.patrick@usdoj.gov. Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Missouri, Eastern

title: Texas residents charged with promoting Illegal tax shelter
body: Press Release Texas residents charged with promoting Illegal tax shelter Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas Caused an estimated tax loss to United States of more than $200 Million – one defendant also charged with fraudulently soliciting $2 million investment in the shelter DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a federal grand jury in Dallas, Texas returned an indictment on Sept. 22, 2026, charging four Texas residents with conspiracy to defraud the United States and other crimes for promoting an illegal tax shelter. According to the indictment, Texas residents Duncan John MacDonald, Sarah Duren, Richard Ronald Cayce and Thomas Weickgenant promoted and sold a fraudulent trust scheme that was used to shelter more than $1.5 billion of income, causing an estimated tax loss to the IRS of more than $200 million. The defendants allegedly sold clients the tax shelter for fees that often exceeded $100,000 by fraudulently telling clients that they could assign their income to sham trusts to defer paying taxes in perpetuity, all while continuing to enjoy the benefit and control over their assets and income. The defendants also allegedly encouraged some clients to backdate their trusts and file amended income tax returns claiming refunds for prior years’ taxes. The indictment also alleges that Weickgenant, who allegedly filed false tax returns for tax shelter clients, obstructed IRS efforts to audit those clients. Weickgenant’s alleged obstruction included instructing clients not to speak with the IRS and encouraging at least one client not to comply with a U.S. District Court order to enforce an IRS summons. The indictment further alleges that MacDonald and Duren, common-law spouses, evaded income taxes on the millions they received in fees from selling the tax shelter. To do so, the couple allegedly concealed MacDonald’s ownership of the tax shelter business and lied to federal investigators. They also allegedly filed false tax returns, used trusts to conceal their receipt of income, and paid personal living expenses through trusts and nominee accounts held in the names of third parties. Allegedly, Cayce, who owned the distributorship licensing the trust tax shelter, likewise received millions of dollars in fees, which he failed to report on his income tax returns. Additionally, according to the allegations, MacDonald fraudulently solicited $2 million from investors to purportedly purchase shares in a business promoting the tax shelter by allegedly developing digital trusts. Instead, MacDonald allegedly used the $2 million to purchase luxury goods for himself, including a Rolls Royce Ghost (pictured below top with MacDonald) and the downpayment for a yacht (pictured below bottom). At the time he received funds from investors, MacDonald allegedly was under a court-ordered injunction prohibiting him from selling securities not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission. MacDonald's Rolls Royce Ghost MacDonald's yacht. The defendants are charged with the following offenses and, if convicted, face the following maximum prison sentences: Count Offense Defendant(s) Maximum Prison Sentence 1 Conspiracy to defraud the United States MacDonald, Duren, Cayce, Weickgenant 5 years 2–6 Aiding in the preparation of a false return MacDonald, Cayce, Weickgenant 3 years per count 7 Corrupt interference with the IRS Weickgenant 3 years per count 8–10 Tax evasion MacDonald 5 years per count 11–13 Duren 14–15 MacDonald, Duren 16–19 Filing a false return Cayce 3 years per count 20–21 Wire fraud MacDonald 20 years per count 22–24 Transactions with criminally derived property MacDonald 10 years per count Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Ryan R. Raybould for the Northern District of Texas made the announcement. IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Eric B. Chen of the Northern District of Texas and Assistant Deputy Chief William Montague and Trial Attorney Max Willner-Giwerc of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section are prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. title: East Hartford Man Charged with Drug Distribution and Gun Possession Offenses
body: Press Release East Hartford Man Charged with Drug Distribution and Gun Possession Offenses Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and P.J. O’Brien, Special Agent in Charge of the New Haven Division of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, today announced that a federal grand jury in New Haven has returned an indictment charging VASHAWN RAY, 38, of East Hartford, with drug distribution and firearm possession offenses. The indictment was returned on October 13, 2026, and Ray was arrested yesterday.  He appeared before U.S. Magistrate Judge Robert A. Richardson in Hartford and was ordered detained As alleged in court documents and statements made in court, on October 25, 2025, Ray and a companion drove a Mercedes SUV to the Westfarms Mall in West Hartford.  While they were inside the mall, a tow truck operator took the vehicle as part of a repossession.  After arriving at the impoundment lot, the tow truck operator found narcotics and a bag containing a firearm in the SUV, and contacted police.  Responding police arrived and recovered approximately 160 wax folds of fentanyl, a quantity of crack cocaine, and a loaded 9mm handgun.  The bag that contained that firearm also contained Ray’s wallet, identification, and credit cards. The indictment alleges that Ray’s criminal history includes state felony convictions for robbery and drug offenses, and a federal conviction in 2013 for a crack cocaine trafficking offense. The indictment charges Ray with possession with intent to distribute fentanyl and cocaine, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 20 years, and unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 15 years. U.S. Attorney Sullivan stressed that an indictment is not evidence of guilt.  Charges are only allegations, and each defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This investigation is being conducted by the FBI’s Northern Connecticut Gang Task Force with the assistance of the Newington and Bloomfield Police Departments.  The Task Force includes members from the Connecticut State Police, the Connecticut Department of Correction, and the East Hartford, Hartford, Manchester, Naugatuck, New Britain, Newington, Waterbury, West Hartford, and Wethersfield Police Departments.  The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Christopher Lembo and Daniel Makofsky. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. title: Brazilian Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Managerial Role in Conspiracy to Launder Tens of Millions of Dollars in Illicit Cash Proceeds
body: Press Release Brazilian Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Managerial Role in Conspiracy to Launder Tens of Millions of Dollars in Illicit Cash Proceeds Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – Ygor Fokin Saviolli, 35, a Brazilian national, was sentenced today to 12 years in prison for his role as a manager and supervisor in a money laundering organization that laundered more than $30 million in illicit proceeds, including the proceeds of drug trafficking. On Sept. 24, five co-defendants received sentences ranging from 94 months in prison to 12 months and one day in prison. Gabriel Cezar Menezes, 29, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 94 months; Omar Aliperti De Mello Correa, 34, a U.S. citizen, was sentenced to 30 months; Leandro De Avila Goncalves, 43, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 24 months; and Joao Andrade De Mello, 29, and Tadeu Sebastiane Rabelo Alves Barbosa, 30, both Brazilian nationals, were each sentenced to 12 months and one day. The Brazilian national defendants were illegally residing in the U.S. at the time of their arrests. “Drug trafficking organizations depend on sophisticated money launderers to turn dirty cash into usable profits,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “Ygor Fokin Saviolli helped manage an international operation that moved and concealed more than $30 million in illicit proceeds, including drug money, across the United States and beyond. We will continue targeting not only the traffickers who poison our communities, but also the financial networks that make their criminal enterprises possible. His sentence of 12 years in federal prison is a consequence of helping turn the proceeds of drug trafficking into the lifeblood of international criminal organizations.” According to court documents, Saviolli, Menezes, Correa, Goncalves, De Mello, and Barbosa were part of a sophisticated money laundering organization that operated across the U.S. and spanned several countries. Members of the conspiracy arranged for U.S.-based couriers to receive bulk cash proceeds from the sale of controlled substances and then to deposit the cash at banks across the country in order to conceal and return those profits to, among others, the sources of drug supply operating outside the U.S. Dozens of pickups across the country were coordinated through WhatsApp message chains that included facilitators and couriers. Saviolli provided upfront funds to facilitate the operations of the money laundering organization and oversaw the receipt and laundering of the bulk cash drug proceeds. Menezes also served as a facilitator, providing direction to and oversight of couriers, and personally picked up bulk cash on multiple occasions. Correa, De Mello, Barbosa, and Goncalves all served as couriers for the money laundering organization, conducting bulk cash pickups in cities including Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, Cleveland, Minneapolis, Rochester, and Tampa, among others. Over the course of the conspiracy, the organization concealed more than $30 million in cash. In June 2026, the defendants’ guilty pleas to conspiracy to commit money laundering were accepted by the district court. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones, and Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement. The FBI investigated the case, with assistance from the Drug Enforcement Administration’s Rochester Resident Office and Homeland Security Investigations’ Brasilia Attaché Office and Miami Field Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Monique Botero for the Southern District of Florida and Trial Attorneys James Hepburn and Jessee Alexander-Hoeppner of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF) prosecuted the case. MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations. MNF’s International Unit investigates and prosecutes cross-border money laundering schemes involving transnational criminal organizations, cartels, foreign official corruption and related money laundering affecting the U.S. financial system and prosecutes criminal cases and civil forfeiture matters to recover the proceeds of those crimes. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case numbers 25-cr-20545. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: North Carolina Man Admits to Producing and Transporting Child Pornography into the United States
body: Press Release North Carolina Man Admits to Producing and Transporting Child Pornography into the United States Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey NEWARK, N.J. – A North Carolina man admitted to producing child pornography in a foreign country and transporting it into the United States, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Barry Grant BeVier, 63, formerly of Wilmington, North Carolina, pleaded guilty on October 14, 2026 before U.S. District Judge Claire C. Cecchi in Newark federal court to an Information charging him with one count of sexually exploiting a child outside the United States for the purpose of producing child pornography and transporting that child pornography into the United States, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 2251(c) and (e). According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: In November 2024, BeVier was outside of the United States and twice persuaded a child to engage in sexually explicit conduct with him by offering the child things of value including a mobile phone.  BeVier filmed videos of himself engaging in the sexually explicit conduct with the child and stored the videos on his cell phone.  He then took an international flight on a commercial airliner into the United States and landed at Newark Liberty International Airport while carrying his cell phone containing the videos.  BeVier also agreed as part of his plea to acknowledge that in November 2024 he produced child pornography involving one additional child. The charge of sexually exploiting a child outside the United States for the purpose of producing child pornography and transporting child pornography into the United States carries a mandatory minimum term of 15 years imprisonment and a maximum term of 30 years imprisonment, and a fine of $250,000. Sentencing is scheduled for February 17, 2027. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy and officers from Customs and Border Protection (CBP), under the direction of New York Director of Field Operation Frank Russo, with the investigation leading to the guilty plea. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) in the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit: https://www.justice.gov/psc . The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Trevor A. Chenoweth of the Cybercrime Unit in Newark. ### Defense counsel: Paul Di Lella, Esq. bevier.information.pdf Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-224

title: Jacksonville Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Drug Offenses
body: Press Release Jacksonville Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Drug Offenses Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Jacksonville, Florida – Jamal Jason James (40, Jacksonville) has been sentenced by Chief U.S. District Judge Marcia Morales Howard to 10 years in federal prison for participating in a drug trafficking conspiracy and possessing MDMA with the intent to distribute it. James pleaded guilty on December 12, 2025. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, on July 29, 2024, members of the Jacksonville Sherriff’s Office responded to Ivy Street in Jacksonville regarding a call for a male lying in the road. When officers arrived, they observed James lying outside the open door of a vehicle used by him. While arranging for aid to tend to James, officers noticed a small bag of a rock-like substance in the vehicle, which laboratory testing later revealed was 6 grams of MDMA, an amount inconsistent with personal use. James was placed in handcuffs and searched. Officers found more than $20,000 in cash on James and inside the vehicle. After James was arrested, he was briefly incarcerated at the Duval County Jail where he made a series of phone calls to Brian Brightman and Anthony Smokes. The calls concerned finding and moving drugs belonging to James being stored in at least one trap house accessible by Brightman and Smokes. They also discussed collecting drug debts owed to James by other members of the conspiracy. In related cases, Brightman and Smokes previously pleaded guilty to federal drug offenses and are awaiting sentencing. This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Nassau County Sherriff’s Office, and the Jacksonville Sherriff’s Office. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Rachel Lasry. Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Fort Thompson Woman Sentenced to 5 Years in Federal Prison  for Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury
body: Press Release Fort Thompson Woman Sentenced to 5 Years in Federal Prison  for Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota PIERRE - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Eric C. Schulte has sentenced a Fort Thompson, South Dakota, woman convicted of Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury.  The sentencing took place on October 5, 2026. Rosilee Grey Owl, 30, was sentenced to five years in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Grey Owl was indicted by a federal grand jury in November 2025. She pleaded guilty on July 1, 2026. On the evening of September 2, 2025, Grey Owl was involved in an argument with the victim, an adult male, at his residence in Fort Thompson, SD, within the Crow Creek Sioux Indian Reservation.  Grey Owl became irate and swung a shovel at the victim, striking him in the head and causing a deep laceration to the back of his head.  The victim was seen by an ambulance crew but refused additional medical help and went back to his room.  The next morning, the victim was found deceased. This matter is being prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office because the Major Crimes Act, a federal statute, mandates that certain violent crimes alleged to have occurred in Indian Country be prosecuted in federal court as opposed to State court. This case is part of the Department of Justice’s Missing or Murdered Indigenous Persons (MMIP) Regional Outreach Program, which aims to aid in the prevention and response to missing or murdered Indigenous people through the resolution of MMIP cases and communication, coordination, and collaboration with federal, Tribal, state, and local partners.  The Department views this work as a priority for its law enforcement components.  Through the MMIP Regional Outreach Program, a broad spectrum of stakeholders work together to identify MMIP cases and issues in Tribal communities and develop comprehensive solutions to address them.  This prosecution upholds the Department’s mission to the unwavering pursuit of justice on behalf of victims and their families despite the passage of time. This case was investigated by the Bureau of Indian Affairs-Office of Justice Services.  Missing and Murdered Indigenous Persons Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Great Plains Troy R. Morley prosecuted the case. Grey Owl was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Component USAO - South Dakota

title: Nashville Man Convicted of Operating Major Cocaine and Fentanyl Trafficking Operation from Downtown Nashville Apartment
body: Press Release Nashville Man Convicted of Operating Major Cocaine and Fentanyl Trafficking Operation from Downtown Nashville Apartment Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Tennessee NASHVILLE – Brandon Ostein, 40, of Nashville, Tennessee, was convicted by a federal jury of multiple drug trafficking and firearms offenses following a jury trial in Nashville, announced United States Attorney for the Middle District of Tennessee Braden H. Boucek. The jury found Ostein guilty of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl and five kilograms or more of cocaine; two counts involving the distribution of cocaine; possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl and five kilograms or more of cocaine; possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime; and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. According to the evidence presented at trial, Ostein operated a large-scale drug trafficking business from an apartment at 1200 Broadway in downtown Nashville. The apartment, served as Ostein’s central location for storing substantial quantities of cocaine and fentanyl, cash, firearms, and equipment used to prepare and package the drugs for distribution. The investigation began in April 2023 and involved controlled purchases of cocaine, physical surveillance, and video recordings. The investigation revealed Ostein’s distribution of cocaine and fentanyl in the Middle Tennessee area. The evidence presented at trial established that Ostein worked with another individual who sold smaller quantities of cocaine while Ostein supplied the cocaine and oversaw the operation. Ostein was also present during several of the cocaine transactions. On August 31, 2023, law enforcement executed a search warrant at the apartment at 1200 Broadway. Inside the apartment, investigators recovered approximately 35 pounds of cocaine, four pounds of fentanyl, $350,000 in cash, and two loaded firearms. Investigators also recovered equipment associated with drug trafficking, including a kilogram press, packaging materials, and other items used in preparing drugs for distribution. The evidence further established Ostein’s access to and control over the apartment through building access records, surveillance footage, and personal belongings recovered inside. Investigators also discovered a telescope positioned toward a nearby parking area, which was used to monitor cocaine deals. The jury convicted Ostein on all counts charged in the indictment. In a separate phase of the trial, the jury also determined that Ostein had qualifying prior felony drug convictions, including Davidson County convictions for possession of more than 300 grams of cocaine, supporting an enhanced statutory penalty. Ostein is set to be sentenced on January 21, 2027, and faces a mandatory minimum sentence of at least thirty years but up to life in prison. The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department, and the Murfreesboro Police Department. Assistant United States Attorneys Juliet Aldridge and Dina A. Shabayek prosecuted the case. ###### Contact Steve Stanley Public Affairs Officer Steve.Stanley2@usdoj.gov (615) 401-6615 Updated October 16, 2026 Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Tennessee, Middle

title: Illegal Alien Sentenced to 13 Years in Prison for 2025 Armed Carjacking, Attempted Carjacking in Philadelphia
body: Press Release Illegal Alien Sentenced to 13 Years in Prison for 2025 Armed Carjacking, Attempted Carjacking in Philadelphia Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Pennsylvania PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Mory Kante, 21, a French national illegally in the U.S., who has been residing in Wilmington, Delaware, was sentenced today to 13 years in prison and five years of supervised release by United States District Judge Gerald J. Pappert for the carjacking and attempted carjacking of two women in one night. The defendant was arrested on a criminal complaint and warrant in January of this year and charged by indictment the same month. He pleaded guilty in June to carjacking, attempted carjacking, and using, carrying, and brandishing a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence. As detailed in court filings, on November 20, 2025, at approximately 9:15 p.m., a woman (“Victim 1”) parked her 2018 Honda Civic on the 1300 block of North Lawrence Street, got out of the vehicle, and walked away. She then saw the defendant run across the street and point a gun at her, saying “gimme your car keys” repeatedly. Victim 1 dropped her purse, and the defendant scooped it up and ran from the scene. Police subsequently found the purse on the street with some of the contents dumped out. Victim 1’s camera, driver’s license, two credit cards, debit card, wallet, and some cash were missing. At approximately 11:00 p.m. that night, police responded to a report of an armed carjacking on the 700 block of West Girard Avenue, approximately seven blocks from where Victim 1 was robbed. A woman (“Victim 2”) reported that a black male wearing all black clothing and a gray hat carjacked her at gunpoint. Victim 2 provided police with location data showing that her car, a 2019 Kia Optima, was near the intersection of Marvin Street and Wyoming Avenue, about four and a half miles north of the carjacking scene. Police located the car and activated their lights and sirens. Kante fled in the vehicle and a brief chase ensued, before the defendant abandoned the car and fled on foot. Pursuing officers saw him toss away a gun, jump on the porch of a nearby residence, and push his way into the home. A SWAT team was called and located the defendant hiding in some bushes in the backyard. This case was investigated by the Philadelphia Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Justin Oshana. title: Georgia Inmates Sentenced in Police‑Impersonation Jury‑Duty Call Scheme
body: Press Release Georgia Inmates Sentenced in Police‑Impersonation Jury‑Duty Call Scheme Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Georgia Inmates Posed as Police, Threatening Citizens and Collecting Payments from Prison ALBANY, Ga. – Two Georgia inmates who orchestrated a phone scheme from behind bars, extorting at least 119 citizens by demanding payment for supposed missed jury‑duty fines, have been sentenced to federal prison following an investigation conducted by the FBI. Lance Riddle, aka “C-Port,” was sentenced to serve a total of 200 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, to run consecutively to any state sentence. Co-defendant Joey Amour Jackson, aka “Apes---,” was sentenced to serve a total of 120 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, to run consecutively to any state sentence. The Court will determine restitution for both defendants in 90 days. Senior U.S. District Judge W. Louis Sands presided over the sentencing hearings on October 14. Jackson and Riddle were found guilty of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering on January 9, after a five-day trial that began on January 5. There is no parole in the federal system. “Even from prison, the defendants preyed on citizens through threats and deceit, scams that too many Americans are confronted with today,” said U.S. Attorney William R. ‘Will’ Keyes. “Our office and our law enforcement partners remain firmly committed to protecting the public and ensuring that those who commit fraud face full accountability.” “Not even prison cells prevented these criminals from harming dozens of innocent people. Hopefully, this sentence will bring some level of comfort to the victims and prevent others from falling for similar scams,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “The FBI will continue to work with our law enforcement partners in not only addressing these types of inmate-based crimes but also in preventing inmates’ access to contraband cell phones that provide the means to do so much harm to the unsuspecting public.” According to court documents and statements referenced at trial, FBI agents in Columbus, Georgia, received information from law enforcement agencies across the U.S. about wire fraud by Georgia inmates, including local law enforcement in Colorado, Florida, Virginia, Nevada, California, and Ohio. Agents discovered that inmates at Calhoun State Prison, including Jackson and Riddle, were using contraband cellular telephones and advanced electronic techniques such as Voice Over Internet Protocol (VOIP) to contact victims from a number that mirrored the numbers of their local police departments. The victims were told they had one or more warrants for their arrest due to missing jury duty. The defendants, posing as police officers, informed the victims that the warrants would be cleared through payment of a bond over the phone and, if not paid, the victims would immediately be arrested. The victims were also informed they were under a “gag” order and couldn’t speak about their warrants until the bond was paid, or they would be immediately arrested. The victims were almost always instructed to buy gift cards and read the numbers off the back of the cards to the defendants, although they sometimes made wire transfers. After paying the bond, victims were instructed to drive to their local police department to verify their signature on the bond. Some victims were told that, because of supposed heightened courthouse security, they needed to go to a local Target store, enter a restroom, undress, and record themselves performing a self-conducted cavity search before verifying their signature. Some victims subsequently received lewd and sexually explicit messages, including violent threats. The scheme primarily targeted female professionals with prominent online profiles, though a small number of male victims were also identified. The inmates impersonated both fictitious individuals and real law enforcement officers from the victims’ local jurisdictions. They worked with co-conspirators outside prison who managed the group’s financial accounts. The stolen proceeds were used to pay off personal debts such as house and vehicle loans, as well as to purchase drugs. The scheme resulted in more than $464,920 in documented losses from 119 victims nationwide, though the true number of victims is likely much higher as many cases go unreported, are not fully investigated, or are concealed by victims who are too embarrassed to come forward. The case was investigated by the FBI Atlanta’s Columbus Resident Agency and prosecuted by Criminal Chief Leah McEwen. title: North Fort Myers Man Pleads Guilty to Illegally Possessing a Gun and Drug Offenses
body: Press Release North Fort Myers Man Pleads Guilty to Illegally Possessing a Gun and Drug Offenses Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Fort Myers, Florida – Olivier Emanuel Fevrier-Sildor (27, North Fort Myers) has pleaded guilty to conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute cocaine, possession with intent to distribute cocaine, possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon, and three counts of distribution of cocaine. He faces up to life imprisonment, a mandatory minimum term of 5 years, consecutive to any other sentence, as well as a $1,000,000 fine. Fevrier-Sildor remains detained pending sentencing. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court records, Fevrier-Sildor was arrested on March 31, 2026, in North Fort Myers, while possessing a distributable quantity of cocaine along with a firearm. Fevrier-Sildor has a prior felony conviction for robbery by sudden snatching. Therefore, he is prohibited from possessing a firearm under federal law. After his arrest and while incarcerated, Fevrier-Sildor recruited Ramiro Jimenez-Flores (20, North Fort Myers) to utilize Fevrier-Sildor’s cell phones and continue to distribute cocaine on his behalf. Law enforcement subsequently conducted three controlled buys of approximately 112 grams of cocaine from Jimenez-Flores on April 10, April 17, and April 29. During the April 29 controlled buy, law enforcement conducted surveillance on Jimenez-Flores as he met up with his source of supply, Christopher Antonio Sierra Lopez (26, Lehigh Acres), and obtained approximately 56 grams of cocaine, which he then sold to an undercover agent. Jimenez-Flores pleaded guilty to conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute cocaine on July 28, 2026. Sierra Lopez pleaded guilty to distribution of cocaine on August 18, 2026. This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Lee County Sheriff’s Office. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Matthew Redavid. title: Justice Department Reaches Settlement Agreement with City of Lexington, Mississippi, Regarding Lexington Police Department’s Unlawful Police Practices
body: Press Release Justice Department Reaches Settlement Agreement with City of Lexington, Mississippi, Regarding Lexington Police Department’s Unlawful Police Practices Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The Justice Department announced today that it has obtained an out-of-court settlement agreement with the City of Lexington, Mississippi, to remedy certain violations described in the Department’s Sept. 26, 2024, findings report. Specifically, the Department found that the Lexington Police Department (LPD) engages in a pattern or practice of civil rights violations. “The Department of Justice supports local law enforcement” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights division. “We are very pleased that the City of Lexington and the Lexington Police Department reached an agreement to enhance the lawful and essential activities of the police department and its officers as they continue to protect and serve the citizens of Lexington and its surrounding areas.” “Today’s agreement reflects a shared commitment to meaningful and sustainable change” said U.S. Attorney J.E. Baxter Kruger for the Southern District of Mississippi. “Through these reforms, we seek not only to address the concerns identified in our investigation, but also to strengthen public trust and promote practices that respect the rights and dignity of every person.” As part of the agreement, the City and LPD will amend policies and practices regarding fines and fees, bail and release criteria, and potential conflict of interests. LPD will also revise its policies and practices regarding stops, searches, arrests, and use of force policies and update its reporting and review of such activities by officers. The Department looks forward to working cooperatively with the City and LPD to ensure that they remedy the alleged violations. The Civil Rights Division’s Special Litigation Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Mississippi initiated the investigation in March 2023 under 34 U.S.C. 12601 which authorizes the Department to take action to remedy a pattern or practice of deprivation of constitutional rights by state or local law enforcement agencies. Additional information about the Civil Rights Division’s work regarding the conduct of law enforcement agencies is available on its website at: www.justice.gov/crt/conduct-law-enforcement-agencies . Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Civil Rights Component Civil Rights Division Press Release Number: 26-1216

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico Announces Creation of the Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico Announces Creation of the Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – Acting United States Attorney Héctor Ramírez Carbó announced the creation of the Puerto Rico Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force, bringing together federal law enforcement agencies, state partners, and inspectors general to strengthen efforts to identify, investigate, and prosecute fraud against government programs and American taxpayers. The U.S. Attorney’s Office hosted the first task force meeting on Thursday, October 15, attended by federal prosecutors and representatives from participating agencies. The meeting focused on establishing an all-hands approach to investigations and prosecutions, expanding intelligence and data sharing, discussing efficient methods for identifying fraud schemes, analysis of investigative leads, and ensuring law enforcement resources are directed toward significant fraud schemes. “Fraud targeting federal government programs steals from taxpayers and deprives intended recipients of essential resources, weakening the impact of programs meant to serve the public,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Héctor Ramírez Carbó. “Our office—working alongside our federal, state, and local partners—will apply every criminal, civil, and administrative tool at our disposal to uncover fraud, stop it, and hold offenders accountable for the harm they cause.” The agencies joining the Puerto Rico Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force include: Federal Bureau of Investigation Homeland Security Investigations U.S. Secret Service Drug Enforcement Administration Office of Inspectors General: IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI) U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General (USPS-OIG) U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) U.S. Small Business Administration Office of Inspector General (SBA-OIG) U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Office of Inspector General (HUD-OIG) U.S. Department of Education Office of Inspector General (Education-OIG) U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General (DOL-OIG) U. S. Department of Agriculture Office of Inspector General (USDA-OIG) Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General (SSA-OIG) Veterans Affairs, Office of Inspector General (VA-OIG) Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division (Army CID) State Partners Puerto Rico Department of Justice (PRDOJ) PRDOJ –  Medicaid Fraud Control Unit (MFCU) Puerto Rico Inspector General The Puerto Rico Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force employs an all‑hands approach and leverages expertise across various federal programs to advance the Department of Justice’s priorities and initiatives. Its mission is to deter fraud, waste, and abuse of federal funds, safeguard taxpayer dollars, and ensure that federal programs reach their intended recipients. Partner agencies will invest all available resources to jointly investigate and prosecute anyone who steals from the American public. These efforts support the U.S. Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative, and creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”), to enhance coordination among federal agencies and strengthen the government’s ability to detect and prosecute fraud. Federal prosecutors and representatives of federal law enforcement agencies, state partners, and inspectors general in the Puerto Rico Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force attended the October 15, 2026, meeting at the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Puerto Rico. ### Updated October 16, 2026 Topics Fraud Benefit Fraud COVID-Related Fraud Disaster Fraud Financial Fraud Healthcare Fraud Mortgage Fraud Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Puerto Rico Press Release Number: 2026-110

title: Oahu Girls’ Wrestling Coach Indicted for Production, Distribution, Receipt, and Possession of Child Pornography and Child Sex Trafficking
body: Press Release Oahu Girls’ Wrestling Coach Indicted for Production, Distribution, Receipt, and Possession of Child Pornography and Child Sex Trafficking Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Hawaii HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Sean Sakaida, 44, of Honolulu, Hawaii, was indicted on October 15, 2026, and charged with four counts of production of child pornography, four counts of distribution of child pornography, one count of receipt of child pornography, four counts of possession of child pornography, and one count of child sex trafficking.  He was previously arrested and taken into custody on September 24, 2026, after being charged by criminal complaint. According to court records, Sakaida, a former coach of the girls’ wrestling team at Moanalua High School, frequently communicated with a minor victim using the messaging application WhatsApp between 2025 and 2026.  In these communications, Sakaida received multiple sexually explicit photographs of the minor victim.  As charged in the indictment, he also produced and distributed multiple videos of himself engaged in sexual acts with the minor victim.  Sakaida was also charged with enticing a second minor victim into engaging in a commercial sex act. If convicted, Sakaida faces at least 15 years and up to 30 years in prison on each production count, at least 5 years and up to 20 years in prison on each distribution and receipt count, up to 10 years in prison on each possession count, up to life in prison on the sex trafficking count, a fine of up to $250,000, plus a term of supervised release. The charges in the indictment are merely accusations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.  In the case of conviction, any sentence would be imposed by a United States District Judge based on the statutory sentencing factors and the advisory United States Sentencing Guidelines. The FBI is investigating the case. Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Heidi Turner is prosecuting the case. The FBI’s Honolulu Field Office is seeking to identify potential victims of Sean Sakaida. If you and/or your minor dependent(s) were victimized by Sean Sakaida or have information relevant to this investigation, please fill out this short form: https://forms.fbi.gov/victims/SakaidaVictims/view If you know of someone else who has possibly been victimized by Sean Sakaida, please encourage them to complete the form themselves. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . title: New York Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Participating in a Nationwide Bank Fraud Conspiracy
body: Press Release New York Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Participating in a Nationwide Bank Fraud Conspiracy Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Alabama MOBILE, AL – A New York man was sentenced to 60 months in prison for participating in a nationwide bank fraud conspiracy involving stolen and counterfeited financial instruments. According to court documents, Curtis Jackson, 31, of Staten Island, New York, admitted that, between February 2023 and June 2024, he conspired with LaEric Marques Williams-Beverly and other conspirators based in Mobile, Alabama, to commit mail theft and bank fraud involving stolen and counterfeited checks. The checks bore the personal identifying information of numerous identity theft victims. Jackson and Williams-Beverly administered an illicit Telegram channel called “House of Pain & Drank,” where millions of dollars’ worth of stolen financial instruments were posted for sale to other fraudsters. In January 2024, agents obtained video footage from a Mobile business (“Business-1”) showing Williams-Beverly stealing checks from the business’s mailbox. Williams-Beverly then coordinated with other coconspirators to counterfeit the checks and fraudulently deposit them into a bank account. ATM surveillance footage captured Williams-Beverly making the fraudulent deposits. Later that month, police in New York City arrested Jackson in possession of a counterfeited check for $43,686.45, drawn on Business-1’s bank account. Jackson had received the check from Williams-Beverly. Jackson’s iCloud account also contained images of stolen and counterfeited checks, including a Citibank deposit slip for a $62,673.46 check drawn on Business-1’s bank account. In June 2024, federal agents executed a search warrant at Williams-Beverly’s home in Mobile. Agents seized numerous pieces of stolen mail, counterfeited checks, debit and credit cards belonging to other individuals, counterfeiting tools, two pistols, and Williams-Beverly’s cell phone. Williams-Beverly admitted to agents that he produced counterfeited checks and coordinated the purchase and sale of stolen checks through the fraudulent Telegram channel he operated with Jackson. Electronic evidence recovered from the conspirators’ cell phones, iCloud accounts, and social media accounts demonstrated the extensive scope of the conspiracy. U.S. District Judge Kristi K. DuBose sentenced Jackson to serve 60 months in federal prison, emphasizing that he was a recidivist with several prior state arrests and convictions for theft, larceny, possession of forged instruments, possession of drugs, and bail jumping. In addition to the five-year prison term, Judge DuBose ordered Jackson to serve a five-year term of supervised release upon his release from prison, during which time he will be subject to drug testing and credit restrictions. The court did not impose a fine, but Judge DuBose ordered Jackson to pay $13,041.52 in victim restitution jointly and severally with Williams-Beverly and other coconspirators, and $100 in special assessments. Williams-Beverly was previously sentenced to 120 months in federal prison for his role in the scheme. U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello of the Southern District of Alabama made the announcement. The United States Postal Inspection Service, the United States Secret Service, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Mobile Police Department, the Jackson Police Department, and the Clarke County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case. The New York City Police Department substantially assisted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Justin Roller prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States. title: Former New Orleans Personal Injury Attorney Sentenced in Connection with Staged Accident Probe
body: Press Release Former New Orleans Personal Injury Attorney Sentenced in Connection with Staged Accident Probe Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – DANNY PATRICK KEATING, JR. , age 57, of New Orleans, was sentenced on October 15, 2026 for Conspiracy to Commit Mail and Wire Fraud, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 371, arising out of staged automobile accidents with tractor-trailers occurring in New Orleans, announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. KEATING was indicted on November 5, 2020, and charged with knowingly engaging in a vast conspiracy involving the intentional staging of motor vehicle collisions with tractor-trailers and commercial vehicles in the metropolitan New Orleans area. Thus far, sixty-three (63) defendants have been charged in the federal probe into the staging of such collisions. KEATING was a personal injury attorney licensed to practice law in Louisiana. At the time of his plea on June 17, 2021, KEATING admitted he knowingly paid Damian Labeaud for thirty-one (31) illegally staged tractor-trailer accidents. KEATING represented seventy-seven (77) plaintiffs involved in the thirty-one (31) accidents staged by Labeaud. KEATING settled seventeen (17) of the thirty-one (31) staged accidents. The indictment charged that KEATING and his clients received a total of approximately $1,500,000.00 in settlement monies resulting from his representation of these clients, and that KEATING kept approximately $358,000.00 of these monies as his attorney’s fees. KEATING admitted filing lawsuits in state and federal court in Louisiana, on behalf of his clients who were involved in the staged accidents. The lawsuits he filed on behalf of the seventy-seven (77) plaintiffs fraudulently misrepresented the identity of the driver of these vehicles, fraudulently misrepresented who was at fault in the staged accidents, and fraudulently claimed injuries. KEATING used the U.S Postal Service to mail settlement demands on behalf of his clients from the Eastern District of Louisiana to various out-of-state locations. In many cases, KEATING ’s clients provided false testimony in depositions taken in conjunction with lawsuits filed by KEATING . United States District Judge Nanette Jolivette Brown sentenced KEATING to thirty-two (32) months of imprisonment, followed by three (3) years of supervised release, as well as the payment of $657,405.34 in restitution, and a $100.00 mandatory special assessment fee. The U.S. Attorney’s Office would like to acknowledge the assistance of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Louisiana State Police, and the Metropolitan Crime Commission with this matter. The prosecution of this case was handled by Brian M. Klebba, Deputy Chief of the Criminal Division and Chief of the Financial Crimes Unit, as well as Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Payne, Edward J. Rivera, Maria Carboni, and U.S. Department of Justice Trial Attorney Ryan J. McLaren. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. 11th Circuit Affirms Conviction, 30-Year Sentence in Cold Case Prosecution of 2001 Murder of Pregnant Army Private in Germany
body: Press Release 11th Circuit Affirms Conviction, 30-Year Sentence in Cold Case Prosecution of 2001 Murder of Pregnant Army Private in Germany Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – The United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the conviction and sentence of Shannon L. Wilkerson, 46, for the 2001 murder of 19-year-old Army Private First Class Amanda Gonzales and her unborn child. In May 2024, a Pensacola jury convicted Wilkerson, a former U.S. solider, of second-degree murder. According to court documents, Wilkerson beat and strangled Gonzales to death on November 3, 2001, in her barracks room at Fliegerhorst Kaserne, then a U.S. Army base in Hanau, Germany. Evidence introduced at trial indicated that Wilkerson feared he was the father of Gonzales’ unborn child and that her pregnancy would interfere with his military career and his marriage to another soldier on the base. Wilkerson was a member of the U.S. Armed Forces at the time of the offense but was later discharged. The district court sentenced Wilkerson to 30 years’ imprisonment. United States Attorney John P. Heekin said: “This cold case prosecution demonstrated the lengths to which my office will go to achieve justice for crime victims.  I am extremely proud that we successfully defended this conviction and sentence against the defendant’s appeal. Nothing can bring back the innocent lives taken by this defendant’s heinous crime, but defending this successful prosecution against his appeal ensures he will not escape accountability.” “This case serves as a perfect example of the Criminal Division’s pursuit of justice no matter the challenge,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division.  “I am proud of the work of the Criminal Division prosecutors, the Northern District of Florida, and the federal agents that worked tirelessly to solve this terrible cold case murder.  I also want to express my deepest condolences to the family of PFC Amanda Gonzales and hope that the affirming of Shannon Wilkerson’s conviction by the Court of Appeals brings some sense of closure to this two-decade pursuit of justice.” Following his conviction and sentencing, Wilkerson appealed to the Eleventh Circuit. After briefing by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida defending the conviction and sentence, the Court rejected each of Wilkerson’s arguments in an unpublished opinion without oral argument. It concluded that the district court acted appropriately in keeping out purely speculative alternative-perpetrator evidence claiming that another soldier committed and pleaded to an unrelated double-homicide in 2006, refusing to entertain the defense’s discovery “fishing expedition” for validation data underlying the government’s DNA evidence, and denying Wilkerson’s motion for a new trial. It likewise found no error in the district court’s conclusion that Wilkerson committed perjury at trial when he denied murdering Gonzales and concluded that Wilkerson had not shown that his 30-year sentence was unreasonable. The Eleventh Circuit’s opinion affirming Wilkerson’s conviction and sentence is available here . The Federal Bureau of Investigation New York and Jacksonville Field Offices investigated this case, with assistance from the Army Criminal Investigative Division. Assistant United States Attorney Jordane New handled the appeal before the Eleventh Circuit. Trial Attorney Patrick Jasperse of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and Assistant United States Attorney David L. Goldberg prosecuted the case. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General.  To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . Contact United States Attorney’s Office Northern District of Florida USAFLN.Press.Office@usdoj.gov X: @USAO_NDFL Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Components Criminal - Human Rights and Special Prosecution Section Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Florida, Northern
