title: Previously Convicted Bank Robber Charged Again for Robbing Banks  Wearing “Old Man” Mask
body: Press Release Previously Convicted Bank Robber Charged Again for Robbing Banks  Wearing “Old Man” Mask Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, Florida – David Sartin, Jr. (40, St. Petersburg) has been charged by criminal complaint with two counts of bank robbery. If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in federal prison on each count. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, on August 24, 2026, Sartin robbed a bank in Largo. On September 15, 2026, he robbed a bank in St. Petersburg. During both robberies, Sartin entered the bank wearing a prosthetic “old man” mask, approached the teller counter and demanded money, and instructed the teller not to include dye packs. The investigation revealed that Sartin had arrived at a nearby gas station shortly before the first robbery, then drove through the surrounding area before parking, switching to a bicycle, and approaching the bank. After the robbery, Sartin fled on the bicycle, retrieved the staged vehicle, and drove away. The vehicle was later seen on multiple nearby roadways heading in the direction of his residence. Video surveillance captured a vehicle leaving Sartin’s home before the second robbery and returning afterwards. When the vehicle returned to the residence, a white male resembling Sartin was seen unloading a bicycle from the vehicle and rolling it toward the residence. The next day, investigators observed Sartin spray paint the vehicle’s white roof black, making the entire vehicle appear black in color. A search of Sartin’s residence uncovered a bicycle, a blue suit, and a black bag, all similar to the items used during the first robbery. A black suit similar to the one used during the second robbery was also recovered. Investigators also seized materials covered in black spray paint and a receipt for clothing purchased the day before the second robbery. A search of Sartin’s storage unit revealed a backpack and laptop bag containing disguise items matching those seen in the surveillance footage from the robberies, including the old‑man mask with grey facial hair, dark‑framed glasses, and work gloves with black paint on them. The bags also contained a fake handgun and clothing consistent with the disguise worn during the second robbery, including a white dress shirt with black studs, a pinstriped sports coat, a dark blue flat cap, and black dress shoes and pants. Agents also searched another residence where Sartin occasionally stayed. There, they found several items, including a prosthetic mask different from the one used in the robberies and a journal titled, “God’s Best friend is a Bank Robber! Uncle Henry Cops and Robbers the world through the eyes of a Bank Robber.” The journal was dated “Jan 1, 2021,” and was “written by: David Sartin.” One of the pages had a drawing of a character holding up a mask along with the handwritten phrase, “My face holding up uncle Henry, looking at it, Face to Face.” At the time of the robberies, Sartin was on supervised release for a 2018 federal conviction stemming from five bank robberies he had committed in Texas in 2016. During these robberies, he wore a similar mask and used the same vehicle he used during the robberies he is charged with now. Sartin was sentenced to 10 years and 1 month in federal prison. Prior to that, in 2008, Sartin was convicted in federal court of attempted bank robbery after he and a co-conspirator had tried robbing a bank wearing Halloween masks and disguises. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Largo Police Department, and the St. Petersburg Police Department. It will be prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Belkis H. Callaos. This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. title: Illegal Alien from Brazil Sentenced for Illegally Reentering the US After Prior Removal
body: Press Release Illegal Alien from Brazil Sentenced for Illegally Reentering the US After Prior Removal Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maine Jose Carlos Ferreira was previously removed in 2010 BANGOR, Maine: A Brazilian national was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Bangor for reentering the United States after a prior removal. U.S. District Judge John A. Woodcock, Jr. sentenced Jose Carlos Ferreria , 50, to time served (59 days). Ferreira pleaded guilty on September 4, 2026. According to court records, on August 15, 2026, U.S. Border Patrol Agents in Franklin County observed a car registered to an alien who had been ordered removed from the United States. During a subsequent roadside immigration inspection, agents determined that the car’s three occupants were, in fact, illegal aliens without lawful authority to be in the country. They were transported for processing to the Rangeley Border Patrol Station, where agents determined that Ferreira had been ordered removed in 2005, and subsequently removed from the U.S. twice in 2010. The U.S. Border Patrol investigated the case. Operation Take Back America : This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. ### Contact Chris Ruge, Assistant United States Attorney (Tel: 207-945-0373) Updated October 16, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Immigration Component USAO - Maine

Three People Charged in Conspiracy to Commit Sex Trafficking of Minors and Related Charges
body: Press Release Three People Charged in Conspiracy to Commit Sex Trafficking of Minors and Related Charges Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs An indictment was unsealed today in the District of Delaware charging Jamar Geeter, 39, of San Francisco, California, Kalvin Carter Jr., 44, of Waldorf, Maryland, and Jada Hasty, 29, of Coatesville, Pennsylvania, with conspiracy to commit sex trafficking of a minor by force, fraud, and coercion, sex trafficking, and coercion and enticement of a minor. Geeter and Hasty are also charged with producing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). “These three individuals are alleged to have exploited and abused four victims — including three children — for their financial gain,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Human trafficking is a serious crime that strips people of their dignity and safety. Anyone who engages in this heinous conduct will be investigated and prosecuted.” “Human-trafficking schemes don’t stop at state lines, and neither does our work to investigate them,” said U.S. Attorney Benjamin L. Wallace for the District of Delaware. “Alongside the Criminal Division and the FBI, my office will pursue anyone charged with exploiting minors in Delaware, no matter where the perpetrators reside.” “According to court documents, Jamar Geeter, already a convicted sex trafficker, continued directing abuse from behind bars with Jada Hasty and Kalvin Carter Jr. as his willing accomplices,” said Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul of FBI Baltimore. “I am proud of the work done by our agents, analysts and victim specialists who handled this case with urgency and care. Their investigation spanned coast- to-coast, rescuing three children and one woman from the clutches of human trafficking and guaranteeing their alleged abusers will feel the full weight of the federal justice system.” According to court documents, Geeter is currently serving a 97-year sentence in California for unrelated state sex trafficking convictions. It is alleged that Geeter used contraband cell phones to engage in some of the alleged criminal conduct while incarcerated. It is also alleged that the defendants conspired to compel three minors and one adult to engage in commercial sex acts in Delaware and elsewhere. Geeter and Hasty recruited, enticed, harbored, transported, provided, obtained, and maintained two minors knowing or in reckless disregard of the fact that they were under the age of 18 and would be caused to engage in commercial sex acts. Geeter and Hasty also used facilities of interstate commerce, including cell phones and the internet, to induce and entice three minors to engage in prostitution. Geeter and Hasty produced CSAM images of two of the minor victims as well. The defendants involved in the scheme used force, threats of force, fraud, or coercion to compel the victims to engage in commercial sex acts. All three defendants are charged with conspiracy to traffic a minor and by force, fraud, and coercion and sex trafficking by force, fraud, or coercion. Geeter and Hasty are also charged with sex trafficking of a minor and by force, fraud, or coercion, coercion and enticement of a minor, and production of CSAM materials. Geeter is charged with additional counts of production and receipt of CSAM materials. If convicted, all three defendants face a minimum penalty of 15 years in prison and a maximum penalty of life in prison on the sex trafficking by force, fraud, and coercion charges. In addition, Geeter and Hasty face a minimum penalty of 15 years in prison and a maximum penalty of life in prison for sex trafficking of a minor charges and coercion and enticement of a minor. Geeter faces a minimum penalty of 25 years in prison and a maximum penalty of 50 years in prison while Hasty faces a minimum penalty of 15 years in prison and a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison on the CSAM charges. The FBI’s Delaware Violent Crime and Safe Streets Task Force and Delaware State Police are investigating the case. Trial Attorney Nicole Raspa of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Claudia Pare for the District of Delaware are prosecuting the case. Anyone who has information about human trafficking should report that information to the National Human Trafficking Hotline toll-free at 1-888-373-7888, which is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For more information about human trafficking, please visit www.humantraffickinghotline.org . Information on the Department of Justice’s efforts to combat human trafficking can be found at www.justice.gov/humantrafficking . An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election and Early Voting in Nevada
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election and Early Voting in Nevada Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada , in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division , announced its comprehensive strategy today to oversee federal voting protections and investigate potential election fraud as early voting begins in Nevada for the 2026 midterm elections . The initiative is part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible voting process. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, alongside federal law enforcement partners, is prepared to enforce federal election laws vigorously while protecting the right of every legal voter to cast their ballot without intimidation or interference. Voters can consult official Department of Justice and state portals to review federal election laws and eligibility requirements. “Maintaining public confidence in our democratic institutions is a top priority. As Nevadans head to the polls for early voting and utilize the state's mail-in ballot options, our office will work hand-in-hand with federal, state, and local partners to safeguard the integrity of the vote. We are committed to a fair election process where every legal ballot is counted accurately. Every single fraudulent, duplicate, or unlawful ballot cast completely cancels out the vote of an honest citizen. Protecting election integrity isn't about keeping people out; it’s about making sure every legal vote counts,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election: Protecting Voter Rights: Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion. Voter Eligibility and Enforcement: Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. For detailed information on ongoing reviews, eligibility laws, or federal penalties, please consult official Department of Justice guidelines and state election authority resources. Combating Election Fraud: Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing. Mail-In and Early Voting in Nevada Nevada state election officials have confirmed that early in-person voting and mail-in voting will proceed as scheduled under standard state protocols. Federal oversight will remain active throughout the early voting period to monitor for compliance with the Voting Rights Act and ensure that secure ballot drop boxes and polling locations are unhindered. Reporting Election Irregularities The public plays a critical role in maintaining election security. Anyone who witnesses or has direct knowledge of potential election fraud, voter intimidation, or unlawful voting activity is strongly encouraged to report it immediately. Please visit the official FBI Tips Portal or contact local law enforcement to report potential election fraud or voting irregularities. Complaints regarding voter discrimination or civil rights violations can also be directed to the Civil Rights Division via the Department of Justice Civil Rights Reporting Portal . ### Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Nevada

title: Mobile Man Sentenced to More Than Five Years in Prison for a Cocaine and Crack Cocaine-Trafficking Conspiracy
body: Press Release Mobile Man Sentenced to More Than Five Years in Prison for a Cocaine and Crack Cocaine-Trafficking Conspiracy Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Alabama MOBILE, AL – A Mobile man was sentenced to 63 months in federal prison for participating in a conspiracy to traffic cocaine and crack cocaine. According to court documents, Rodney Antwaine Davis, 42, was arrested on November 9, 2023, after leading police officers on a high-speed chase through a residential neighborhood in Mobile. Davis crashed into a ditch and attempted to flee on foot but was apprehended by officers. During the arrest, officers seized $6,145 in cash and a plastic bag containing crack cocaine from Davis’s underwear. A chemist confirmed that the crack cocaine weighed 52.69 grams. On March 20, 2025, federal agents obtained a warrant to search a package mailed from Houston, Texas, to an address on Johnston Street in Mobile under a fictitious name. The package contained more than two kilograms of vacuum-sealed powder cocaine and a bottle containing 300 alprazolam pills, as confirmed by laboratory testing. The following day, an undercover agent delivered the package to the residence on Johnston Street. Davis arrived and retrieved the package. Agents moved in to arrest him, but Davis fled into the house before being apprehended in a bedroom. At the time of his arrest, Davis had $5,734 in cash in his pocket. Agents also discovered a small amount of methamphetamine on a bed near where Davis was arrested and three bottles of promethazine syrup in Davis’s car, which was parked outside the residence. Agents seized and searched Davis’s cell phone, which contained messages and other data related to his drug-trafficking conspiracy. U.S. District Judge Kristi K. DuBose sentenced Davis to a total of 63 months in prison, with his sentence adjusted to account for the 19 months he has spent in custody since March 2025. Upon his release from prison, Davis will serve four years of supervised release, during which he will be subject to drug testing. The ordered Davis to pay $100 in special assessments. U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello of the Southern District of Alabama made the announcement. Homeland Security Investigations, the United States Postal Inspection Service, the Mobile Police Department, and the Mobile County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Justin Roller prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States. Updated October 16, 2026 Component USAO - Alabama, Southern

title: Shiprock Man Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for Second-Degree Murder
body: Press Release Shiprock Man Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for Second-Degree Murder Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Shiprock man was sentenced to 20 years in prison for fatally stabbing a man in broad daylight near a community grocery store in Shiprock, New Mexico. According to publicly available court documents, on the afternoon of July 25, 2024, officers with the Navajo Nation Police Department responded to a fight in progress near a high-traffic Navajo Nation shopping center in Shiprock, New Mexico. Upon arrival, they found a man lying on the ground with wounds to his face and chest. Witnesses reported that Edison Brady , 57, an enrolled member of the Navajo Nation, had stabbed the man in the chest after the man was already badly beaten, hardly conscious, lying on the ground, and bleeding from the head. According to multiple witnesses, Brady attacked the victim without provocation, repeatedly punching and kicking him as he remained on the ground and attempted to shield his face. Brady then walked away, retrieved a long kitchen knife from his nearby bag, and returned to stab the victim in the chest as the victim lay bleeding and barely conscious. The victim died from his injuries shortly after arriving at the Northern Navajo Medical Center. Officers recovered the knife, which was covered in the victim’s blood, from Brady ’s bag minutes after the attack. Brady pleaded guilty without a plea agreement to an indictment charging him with one count of second-degree murder. Upon his release from prison, Brady will be subject to five years of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. Brady must also compensate the New Mexico Crime Victim Reparations Commission for the $6,000.00 it expended paying for the victim’s funeral expenses. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the FBI’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Farmington Resident Agency of the FBI’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from Navajo Nation Police Department and Navajo Nation Department of Criminal Investigations. Assistant United States Attorneys Jena Ritchey and Zachary C. Jones are prosecuting this case. title: Philadelphia Man Convicted for his Role in a $2 Million Theft
body: Press Release Philadelphia Man Convicted for his Role in a $2 Million Theft Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey CAMDEN, N.J. – A Philadelphia man was convicted on October 15, 2026, for his role in stealing $2 million from a Glassboro business and laundering the proceeds of his theft, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Ruben Cruz, 33, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and Davenport, Florida, was convicted of one count of conspiracy to transport stolen property across state lines, one count of interstate transportation of stolen property, one count of conspiracy to launder money, and seven counts of money laundering.  Cruz was convicted following a three-day trial before U.S. District Judge Christine P. O’Hearn in Camden federal court.  Sentencing is set for February 24, 2027. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial: Over the 2021 July 4 th holiday weekend, Cruz and co-conspirator Ricky Rivas-Ortiz burglarized a Glassboro business, stealing a safe that contained more than $2 million in money orders and cash and taking it to Philadelphia.  After the burglary, Cruz and another co-conspirator negotiated money orders from the stolen safe in a manner designed to conceal that they were stolen.  One method they used to launder the proceeds was altering the stolen money orders and depositing them in piecemeal fashion.  For example, Cruz deposited some of the stolen money orders on the same day at different banks that were next door to each other and deposited other stolen money orders at the same bank branch over several consecutive days. Rivas-Ortiz previously pleaded guilty to an information charging him with transporting stolen property interstate and was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Christine P. O’Hearn to 21 months’ imprisonment. For Cruz, the count of conspiracy to transport stolen property interstate carries a maximum penalty of 5 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000, or twice the gross loss to the victim or gain to the defendant, whichever is greatest.  The count of interstate transportation of stolen property carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000, or twice the gross loss to the victim or gain to the defendant, whichever is greatest.  The count of conspiracy to launder money and each money laundering count carry a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison and a fine of up to $500,000, or twice the value of the laundered money, whichever is greatest. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited postal inspectors of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Philadelphia Division, under the direction of Inspector in Charge Christopher A. Nielsen, and agents of the Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation, Newark Field Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Jenifer L. Piovesan, with the investigation leading to the convictions.  He also thanked the Gloucester County Prosecutor’s Office, under the direction of Prosecutor Andrew B. Johns, and the Elk Township Police Department, under the direction of Chief Lance Hitzelberger, for their valuable assistance in the case. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jeffrey Bender and Joseph McFarlane of the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Camden. 26-225                                                                         ### Defense counsel: Brian O’Malley, Haddon Township, New Jersey. cruz.supersedingindictment.pdf Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-225

U.S Departments of Justice and Labor Secure Settlement with Cloudera, Enforce Two-Year PERM Debarment & Back Pay Following Discrimination Against U.S. Workers
body: Press Release U.S Departments of Justice and Labor Secure Settlement with Cloudera, Enforce Two-Year PERM Debarment & Back Pay Following Discrimination Against U.S. Workers Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The U.S. Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division (CRT) and the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) today announced a coordinated enforcement resolution with Cloudera Inc., a Santa Clara, California-based data management company, following allegations that the company discriminated against qualified U.S. workers during recruitment conducted under the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program. “There are no exceptions: the Justice Department will hold accountable employers who discriminate against U.S. workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This substantial settlement, in partnership with DOL, sends a strong signal to employers that the federal government will work together to ensure employers treat U.S. workers fairly.” As part of the resolution, Cloudera will be barred from participating in the PERM program for two years, one of the most significant sanctions available for DOL to protect the integrity of the employment-based immigration system and safeguard opportunities for U.S. workers. The debarment follows DOL’s earlier suspension of Cloudera’s PERM processing and reflects DOL’s commitment to aggressively enforcing labor certification requirements when employers fail to provide U.S. workers a fair opportunity to compete for jobs. The settlement also resolves a lawsuit DOJ filed in April of this year, alleging that Cloudera violated the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) by discriminating against U.S. workers when recruiting and hiring for seven positions under the PERM process. Under the terms of the settlement with the Justice Department, Cloudera will establish a back-pay fund of $1.4 million to compensate qualified U.S. workers who tried to apply for the jobs at issue but were not given fair consideration. Cloudera also will pay $600,000 in civil penalties to the United States. In addition to the two-year debarment, Cloudera will be subject to compliance obligations designed to ensure future adherence to federal labor and anti-discrimination laws. These measures include enhanced monitoring, revised PERM compliance procedures, and reporting requirements intended to prevent future violations. This debarment and compliance framework establish an important enforcement precedent and strengthen future efforts to protect U.S. workers. The PERM program allows employers to sponsor aliens for permanent residence only after demonstrating that qualified U.S. workers were provided a genuine opportunity to apply and that no qualified, willing, and available U.S. workers could be found. Employers who evade these requirements undermine both program integrity and the interests of U.S. workers. This resolution is one of many examples of coordinated federal enforcement designed to ensure employers comply with labor market protections established by Congress. This settlement is also the fourteenth settlement since DOJ re-launched its Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative in 2025 to enforce the INA’s prohibition on citizenship status discrimination against companies that illegally discriminate against U.S. workers in favor of those with temporary employment visas. Under these settlements, DOJ obtains civil penalties for each violation and will continue to appropriately seek the maximum penalty permitted by law. The settlements also involve awards of back pay, when warranted, and require employers to conduct comprehensive training for relevant staff and recruiters and cease restricting consideration for job opportunities based on workers’ citizenship status without a lawful reason. For information about additional settlements under the Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative, visit IER’s website . For informal assistance, the public can call IER’s free hotline at 1-800-255-7688 for workers or at 1-800-255-8155 for employers (1-800-237-2515, TTY for hearing impaired) between 9am and 5pm Eastern Time, Monday through Friday; sign up for a live webinar or watch an on-demand presentation ; email IER@usdoj.gov ; or visit www.justice.gov/ier . title: Five Non-Citizens Arrested for Voter Fraud Across the Northern District
body: Press Release Five Non-Citizens Arrested for Voter Fraud Across the Northern District Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On October 13 and 14, 2026, Vikki Bradt, age 51, a British National, of Ballston Spa, NY, Samantha Merkle, age 55, a British National of Glens Falls, NY, Suad Sasic, age 30, a Bosnian National of Clifton Park, NY, Jacques Patry, age 64, a Canadian National of Tupper Lake, NY, and Paula Stitt, age 57, a Canadian National of Albany, NY, appeared on charges of voting by aliens. All defendants are lawful permanent residents. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Anthony Patrone, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) made the announcement. The complaints against all five defendants allege that they are aliens, who knew they were not United States citizens and that they knowingly voted in an election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, Member of the United States Senate, or Member of the United States House of Representatives. These charges carry a maximum sentence of one year in prison and a fine up to $100,000.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute(s) the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines, and other factors. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated, “the law is clear that only U.S. citizens can vote in elections that have candidates running for federal office.  When non-citizens vote, the public loses confidence in the integrity of the election process and its outcome.  Our office, working with our federal law enforcement partners, will work tirelessly to prosecute those who should not have voted, but did.  Just this week, our office filed charges against five individuals, all of whom were non-citizens and unlawfully voted in federal elections within the last few years.” "The integrity of lawful voting and government processes is essential to maintaining public confidence in our institutions," said Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Buffalo Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony J. Patrone." From the North Country to the Capital Region, residents expect that the systems affecting their communities, including the electoral process, operate fairly, lawfully, and with accountability. Today’s charges reflect that coordinated effort and HSI's commitment to investigate alleged voter fraud and protect the integrity of government processes that communities in this region rely upon." The charges in the complaints are merely accusations. The defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Richard Belliss and Benjamin Loefke are prosecuting the case. Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Two Plead Guilty to Unemployment Insurance Benefits Fraud Conspiracy
body: Press Release Two Plead Guilty to Unemployment Insurance Benefits Fraud Conspiracy Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Las Vegas residents Ricky Lee Ware, 43, and Kimberly Ann Wallace, 30, pleaded guilty today to conspiracy to commit access device fraud, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. According to court documents, between July 2020 and January 2021, the defendants conspired to obtain debit cards that allowed them to access unemployment benefits. The unemployment benefits were in the names of people who did not know the defendants. The defendants then used the debit cards to withdraw more than $900,000 in unemployment benefits from ATMs. The U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General, Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation; and the Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas M. Fogg is prosecuting the case. Ware and Wallace are scheduled to be sentenced by U.S. District Judge Dena Coggins on Feb. 19, 2027, and face a maximum of 7.5 years in prison. The actual sentence, however, will be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The third defendant in the case, Carlos Lee Sanchez Jr., 46, of Sacramento, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit access device fraud in June 2026 and is scheduled to be sentenced Nov. 13, 2026. This effort is part of a California COVID-19 Fraud Enforcement Strike Force operation, one of five interagency COVID-19 fraud strike force teams established by the U.S. Department of Justice. The California Strike Force combines law enforcement and prosecutorial resources in the Eastern and Central Districts of California and focuses on large-scale, multistate pandemic relief fraud perpetrated by criminal organizations and transnational actors. The strike forces use prosecutor-led and data analyst-driven teams to identify and bring to justice those who stole pandemic relief funds. title: D.C. Mother Pleads Guilty to Perjury for Lying to Grand Jury During Investigation into Her 2-Year-Old Son’s Murder
body: Press Release D.C. Mother Pleads Guilty to Perjury for Lying to Grand Jury During Investigation into Her 2-Year-Old Son’s Murder Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov WASHINGTON – Monet Jones, 28, of Washington, D.C., pleaded guilty today for lying to the grand jury about the beating death of her 2-year-old child, Mars Jones, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “Two-year-old Mars deserved a mother who would fight for justice, not protect the man who beat her child to death,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Instead, she misled investigators and deleted evidence to shield him from accountability. If you obstruct justice to protect someone who kills a child, you will answer for it. No exceptions.” Jones pleaded guilty before D.C. Superior Court Judge Rainey Brandt to one count of perjury and one count of tampering with evidence. Judge Park scheduled sentencing for February 1, 2027, with her co-defendant, Dasean Matthews. According to the government’s evidence, on October 13, 2022, 2-year-old Mars, Jones, and Matthews, (co-defendant Jones’s romantic partner) drove to a Dunkin Donuts just before noon. While in the Dunkin Donuts, video evidence shows Matthews striking the young child with a closed fist in the upper body causing Mars to fall and slam against a metal railing. Later that day, while in a parking garage, video evidence shows Matthews grabbing Mars by the neck of his clothing, swing him by the clothing, and minutes later, strike Mars in the upper body or face, causing the young child to again fall to the floor. Later the same day, while alone in a vehicle with Mars, video evidence shows defendant Matthews repeatedly strike the young child so forcefully that the vehicle shakes from the impact of the blows. Immediately thereafter, Matthews delivers an unconscious and bloody baby Mars to Jones and then flees the scene. An autopsy determined that Mars died from complications of inflicted head trauma. Throughout the pendency of the case, Jones repeatedly lied to law enforcement and the grand jury about witnessing defendant Matthews’ assaulting her child or being in the Dunkin Donuts on October 13, 2022, in an attempt to hinder the investigation. Jones also deleted messages between her and Matthews from her phone in an attempt to protect Matthews. Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department. This case was investigated by the Special Victims Unit of the Homicide Section at the Metropolitan Police Department and was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Emma McArthur and Shauna Payyappilly. 2023 CF2 000873 Contact USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Waipahu Women Sentenced to Two Years in Prison for Pandemic and Tax Fraud While Earning Millions from an Unlicensed Construction Business
body: Press Release Waipahu Women Sentenced to Two Years in Prison for Pandemic and Tax Fraud While Earning Millions from an Unlicensed Construction Business Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Hawaii HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Heidi Cafirma, 46, of Waipahu, Hawaii, was sentenced on September 30, 2026, by United States District Judge Shanlyn A.S. Park to 24 months in prison followed by 3 years of supervised release for filing false tax returns and wire fraud.  Cafirma was also ordered to forfeit $70,500 and pay up to over $1 million in restitution, which total amount will be determined by the court at a later date.  Cafirma pled guilty pursuant to a plea agreement in December 2025. In 2020, the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act created the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA) unemployment insurance program to provide emergency unemployment payments to certain workers whose livelihoods were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic but who were ineligible for traditional state unemployment insurance benefits, such as business owners, self-employed workers, independent contractors, and those with a limited work history who were out of business or had significantly reduced their services as a direct result of the pandemic.  To obtain either traditional unemployment insurance (UI) or PUA UI benefit payments, claimants could submit a claim online.  If approved, the U.S. Treasury typically deposited payments every week into a claimant’s bank account.  To continue to receive benefit payments, claimants were required to certify on a weekly basis under penalty of law that they remained unemployed or partially employed, and eligible to receive benefit payments. According to court documents, Cafirma admitted that between June 2020 and September 2021, she submitted 22 false claims online for UI benefit payments for herself by repeatedly falsely certifying under penalty of law that she was unemployed and not receiving income, despite knowing that her certifications were false because she received over $1 million in income during that period from her and her husband’s unlicensed construction business.  Cafirma fraudulently obtained at least $70,500 in unemployment insurance and PUA UI benefits to which she was not entitled. Between 2016 and 2020, Cafirma also willfully failed to pay federal and state taxes on over $3.4 million in income from her and her husband’s construction business.  She provided false documents to her tax return preparer that omitted income and then filed false tax returns with the IRS.  Over at least four years, Cafirma took steps to conceal her income by directing construction customers to write checks to her personally rather than to her business, funneling income through sixteen bank accounts at multiple financial institutions, and structuring multiple cash deposits in amounts less than $10,000 to avoid banks from filing of currency transaction reports. “Bringing to justice criminals like Cafirma – who defraud the government, divert critical and limited resources to themselves out of greed, and steal from hardworking, taxpaying citizens – remains one of my office’s top priorities,” said United States Attorney Ken Sorenson.  “We will continue to leverage our resources and those of the National Fraud Enforcement Division to investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars.” “Ms. Cafirma’s pattern of fraud has caught up to her with today’s sentencing.  Not only did she lie to fraudulently underpay her fair share of taxes, Ms. Cafirma also stole funds meant to help others in the community that truly needed the assistance,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge Jay Gregory, IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), Seattle Field Office.  “IRS-CI is committed to protecting our communities and the financial systems we all rely on, and we will continue to investigate criminals like Ms. Cafirma.” The IRS – Criminal Investigation investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Rebecca A. Perlmutter prosecuted the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”).  The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people.  The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. Contact Aislinn Affinito Aislinn.Affinito@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Topics COVID-Related Fraud Financial Fraud Component USAO - Hawaii

title: Massachusetts Man Charged for His Role in Marriage and Immigration Document Fraud
body: Press Release Massachusetts Man Charged for His Role in Marriage and Immigration Document Fraud Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio CLEVELAND – A 31-year-old man has been charged for his role in a conspiracy where he allegedly agreed to be paid to enter into a sham marriage to allow a co-conspirator to illegally obtain a green card. A federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Jingming Chen, 31, of Quincy, Massachusetts, with Conspiracy to Commit Marriage Fraud and Immigration Document Fraud. According to allegations in the indictment, Chen, a U.S. citizen, was paid by a Chinese national co-conspirator residing in Aurora, Ohio, to enter into a sham marriage and commit immigration document fraud by fabricating evidence to support the false claim that their marriage was legitimate. They submitted false statements to the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Service (USCIS) to obtain lawful permanent resident status—commonly known as a Green Card—and other immigration benefits for the co-conspirator. To carry out the conspiracy, Chen allegedly agreed to receive partial payment at each step of the green card process as they were completed. Chen and the co-conspirator discussed creating a false backstory of their online romance and long-distance relationship, including how they met and who introduced them. They also went so far as to discuss obtaining a prenuptial agreement and opening various joint accounts for banking, cellphone service, insurance, and a discount store membership card. Eventually, the two filed an intent to get married in Quincy, Massachusetts, and Chen directed the co-conspirator to buy a cheap, fake diamond ring to use for the wedding ceremony.  After they married, Chen directed a preparer to submit his USCIS Form I-130, “Petition for Alien Relative,” to document his relationship with a foreign national which would pave the way for the co-conspirator to obtain a green card. The Homeland Security Investigations Cleveland office and the USCIS-Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate in Boston conducted the investigation preceding the indictment. Assistant United States Attorney Brian M. McDonough is leading the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. If convicted, the defendant faces up to five years in prison. The court will determine the sentence after reviewing the factors unique to this case, including the defendant’s prior criminal record, if any, the defendant’s role in the offenses, and the characteristics of the violations. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The Fraud Division investigates and prosecutes those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. An indictment is merely an allegation. A defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Contact Jessica Novak jessica.salas.novak@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Topics Fraud Immigration Component USAO - Ohio, Northern

title: Connecticut Physician and His Practices Pay More Than $860K to Settle False Claims Act Allegations
body: Press Release Connecticut Physician and His Practices Pay More Than $860K to Settle False Claims Act Allegations Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut STEVEN MURPHY, M.D. and his practices, MURPHY MEDICAL ASSOCIATES, LLC and DIAGNOSTIC AND MEDICAL SPECIALISTS OF GREENWICH, LLC, located in Stamford, have entered into a civil settlement agreement with the federal and state governments in which they will pay $866,539 to settle allegations of COVID-19 related fraud and health care fraud.  As part of the settlement, Murphy and his practices agreed to be excluded from all federal health care programs for a period of three years. The government alleges that Murphy and his practices submitted false and fraudulent claims to the Health Resources Services Administration (HRSA), which is a sub-agency of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, to reimburse Murphy for “uninsured” patients treated during the COVID-19 pandemic.  The government also alleges that Murphy submitted false claims to Medicaid and Medicare for blood testing “panels” allegedly performed by Murphy’s in-house lab. COVID-19 Uninsured Program Fraud In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, Congress passed a series of bills to provide funds to health care providers for COVID-19 testing and treatment for uninsured individuals (the “Uninsured Program”).  The Uninsured Program reimbursed eligible health care providers for COVID-19 testing, treatment, and vaccine administration provided to uninsured individuals.  HRSA was selected to provide oversight and management of the Uninsured Program. An uninsured individual was defined as someone who was “not enrolled” in a government or private health insurance program as of the date of service in question.  Prior to seeking reimbursement from the Uninsured Program, health care providers were required to attest to the government that they had confirmed that the patients for whom they were seeking reimbursement were uninsured. Murphy and his practices participated in the Uninsured Program, attested that the patients for whom they sought payment were uninsured, and received reimbursement from the Uninsured Program for those patients.  The government alleges that Murphy and his practices had information, including copies of insurance cards and other documents, in their files indicating that certain patients for which they made attestations and submitted claims for reimbursement to the Uninsured Program were, in fact, enrolled in government or private health insurance programs.  In addition, Murphy and his practices changed the patient’s insurance identifying information to “Covid19 HRSA Uninsured” in their internal electronic medical records system and then submitted claims and received reimbursement from the Uninsured Program for those patients. Blood Testing Fraud Murphy had an in-house lab that performed blood tests on patients.  The lab performed blood tests on patients who had possible exposure to COVID-19 or were presenting with COVID-19 symptoms, and also performed blood tests on non-COVID patients, including those who were having an annual physical exam. Murphy and his practices utilized blood testing panels in their in-house lab.  The blood testing panels were not billed and paid at one price per panel.  Each blood test that made up the panel was billed separately to Medicare or Medicaid. Reagents were used to run the specific blood tests that made up the panel, but there were times when Murphy and his practices failed to purchase certain reagents or otherwise did not have certain reagents, so they could not run the complete blood testing panel.  The government alleges that Murphy and his practices billed Medicare and Medicaid for specific blood tests that were part of their standard panel, but which were never actually performed, because they did not have the reagents necessary to perform the specific blood tests that were billed. To resolve the governments’ federal and state False Claims Act allegations, Murphy and his practices have agreed to pay $866,539, which covers the time-period from September 2019 through April 2022.  Murphy and his practices also agreed to be excluded from all federal health care programs for a period of three years. This matter was investigated by the Office of Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.  The matter was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorney Richard M. Molot, with the assistance of Auditor Susan Spiegel, and by Deputy Associate Attorney General Gregory O’Connell of the Connecticut Office of the Attorney General. People who suspect health care fraud are encouraged to report it by calling 1-800-HHS-TIPS or the Health Care Fraud Task Force at (203) 777-6311. Updated October 16, 2026 Topics COVID-Related Fraud Healthcare Fraud Component USAO - Connecticut

title: Tucson Man Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for Child Exploitation Crimes
body: Press Release Tucson Man Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for Child Exploitation Crimes Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona TUCSON, Ariz. – A Tucson man will spend two decades in prison after fueling an international child-exploitation ring that broadcasted the real-time abuse of minors. On Oct. 14, David Berry Garmarnik, 48, of Tucson, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Rosemary Marquez to 20 years in prison. Garmarnik previously pleaded guilty to one count of Attempted Production of Child Pornography. “Live‑streamed child sexual abuse is one of the most urgent and devastating forms of exploitation, and offenders who fuel it will be met with swift, aggressive, and unrelenting prosecution,” said U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine. “These crimes inflict real‑time harm on real children, and our office will pursue anyone who participates in this abuse, no matter where they hide or how they operate. We are grateful to HSI for its relentless work in dismantling international trafficking networks and for ensuring that those who prey on children are brought to justice.” “This case demonstrates the devastating reality of child exploitation, and the lengths offenders will go to abuse children and conceal their crimes. HSI is committed to identifying these offenders, dismantling the networks that enable their abuse, and working with our domestic and international law enforcement partners to ensure they are held accountable. Protecting children and pursuing those who exploit them remains a priority for HSI, wherever these crimes lead us,” said Jason Stevens, Special Agent in Charge of HSI Phoenix. According to the plea agreement, Garmarnik admitted that he requested and directed sexually explicit conduct of children under the age of 12 and in some cases as young as 7. Additional court records show that HSI identified David Berry Garmarnik as a participant in an international child‑exploitation network that live‑streamed the sexual abuse of minors for paying offenders around the world. Investigators linked Garmarnik to more than 100 online interactions with known or suspected traffickers between 2017 and 2022. Records obtained from Microsoft showed thousands of messages, media files, and call logs consistent with child‑exploitation activity. In addition, financial subpoenas revealed that Garmarnik sent over 100 payments to individuals in the Philippines with no legitimate connection to him, including a known trafficker whose operation involved the abuse of children as young as two years old. After search warrants were executed, Garmarnik admitted he had paid for approximately 100 live‑streamed shows involving minors. He also acknowledged downloading child sexual abuse material and communicating with traffickers using his Skype account. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . Homeland Security Investigations – Tucson conducted the investigation in this case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Nathaniel J. Walters and Jennifer H. Berman, District of Arizona, Tucson, handled the prosecution. title: New Jersey Man Indicted on Arson Charges Connected to Retail Store Fire
body: Press Release New Jersey Man Indicted on Arson Charges Connected to Retail Store Fire Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Baltimore, Maryland – A New Jersey man is facing indictment, today, after using fire and explosive materials in a Maryland retail store. Anthony John Rhodes, 37, of Short Pump, is charged with malicious destruction of property by fire. The charges stem from an incident in which Rhodes set a fire in an Elkton retail store during business hours while customers shopped. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Chief Caroll H. Spriggs, II, Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal. According to the indictment, on April 29, 2026, Rhodes maliciously damaged and destroyed the store building, along with its merchandise and inventory. An indictment is not a finding of guilt.  Individuals charged by indictment are presumed innocent until proven guilty at a later criminal proceeding. If convicted, Rhodes faces a minimum of five years and a maximum of 20 years in federal prison.  Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal for their work in the investigation, along with Office of the State’s Attorney for Cecil County, for its valuable assistance.  Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Victoria Liu who is prosecuting the federal case. title: St. Louis County Man Admits Using Fraudulent Deed Filings to Steal At Least 14 Properties
body: Press Release St. Louis County Man Admits Using Fraudulent Deed Filings to Steal At Least 14 Properties Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri ST. LOUIS – A man on Thursday admitted conspiring to steal at least 14 properties in St. Louis and St. Louis County by filing fraudulent deeds. James L. Townes Jr., 51, of Berkeley, pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to a conspiracy charge. Townes admitted that beginning as early as Sept. 25, 2018, he began filing fraudulent deeds in St. Louis and St. Louis County on properties that belonged to others. The filings falsely claimed that Townes or his relatives had purchased the properties. Townes and his co-defendant, Charnay Bartlett, used fraudulently obtained notary seals to “authenticate” the forged signatures of the true owners of the properties. Townes and Bartlett transferred at least 14 properties to Townes, his companies or his friends and family, his plea agreement says. Townes admitted that his scheme involved the use of the names of 10 or more individuals and that the intended losses associated with his actions exceeded $1,500,000. The real owners had to expend considerable resources to regain the titles to their properties. Others abandoned their properties because they lacked the financial resources to initiate legal action. At least three of the property owners were deceased at the time when their purported signatures were authenticated by Townes and Bartlett. In some cases, Townes gained access to the properties by forcing entry through locked doors and squatting there. Bartlett, 30, pleaded guilty in April to the same conspiracy charge and is scheduled to be sentenced on December 2. Townes is set to be sentenced on January 21. The charge carries a penalty of up to five years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000 or both prison and a fine. The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Office of Inspector General, the Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General, the St. Louis County Police Department and the Hazelwood Police Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Gwen Carroll is prosecuting the case. Contact Robert Patrick, Public Affairs Officer, robert.patrick@usdoj.gov. Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Missouri, Eastern

title: Twice-Deported Illegal Alien from Mexico Arrested on Federal Complaint Charging Him with Possessing 360 Kilograms of Cocaine
body: Press Release Twice-Deported Illegal Alien from Mexico Arrested on Federal Complaint Charging Him with Possessing 360 Kilograms of Cocaine Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of California RIVERSIDE, California – A twice-deported illegal immigrant from Mexico has been arrested on a federal criminal complaint charging him with possessing approximately 360 kilograms (793.7 pounds) of cocaine in his San Bernardino County apartment, the Justice Department announced today. José María Mena Rosales, 38, of Fontana, was arrested on Wednesday and is charged with possession with intent to distribute cocaine. Rosales made his initial appearance on Thursday in United States District Court in Riverside. United States Magistrate Judge David T. Bristow ordered Rosales released on $50,000 bond. No plea was taken. Rosales’s arraignment is scheduled for November 10. According to an affidavit filed with the complaint, in February 2026, law enforcement investigating a Mexico-based drug trafficking organization learned that a large quantity of cocaine was to be delivered in four suitcases to Rosales at a public parking lot in Fontana. Rosales later retrieved the cocaine from the parking lot and drove to his apartment, where he unloaded the suitcases of narcotics into a garage. Law enforcement executed a search warrant at Rosales’s garage and apartment and seized approximately 360 kilograms of cocaine spread across 17 cardboard boxes. The four empty suitcases were found in the garage. Law enforcement officers confirmed Rosales’s identity with his California driver’s license and found several cell phones that contained text messages between Rosales and the individual who arranged the cocaine delivery. According to court documents, Rosales was deported from the United States in May 2014 and June 2014. A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. If convicted, Mena would face a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in federal prison and a statutory maximum sentence of life in federal prison. The FBI is investigating this matter with assistance from the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department. Assistant United States Attorney Courtney N. Williams of the Transnational Organized Crime Section is prosecuting this case. Contact Ciaran McEvoy Public Information Officer ciaran.mcevoy@usdoj.gov (213) 894-4465 Updated October 16, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Immigration Component USAO - California, Central Press Release Number: 26-199

title: Two Florida defendants sentenced to prison for nearly $900,000 health care scam
body: Press Release Two Florida defendants sentenced to prison for nearly $900,000 health care scam Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas TOPEKA, KAN. – Two defendants received prison sentences following an $897,405 health care scheme where they used their pharmaceutical service to bill Medicare for thousands of unnecessary and illegal prescriptions. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. According to court documents, the following defendants pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit health care fraud, mail fraud, and wire fraud: Steven Anthony Churchill, 39, of Boca Raton, Florida, was sentenced to 24 months in prison; Samson Kollelil Solomon, 28, of Pompano Beach, Florida, was sentenced to 24 months in prison; and Fawn Lickteig, 46, of Lawrence, Kansas, will be sentenced on November 10, 2026. In March 2020, Steven Churchill bought Free State Pharmacy (FSP) in Lawrence, Kansas, but under the name of a now deceased, accused coconspirator. FSP operated as a mail-order pharmacy despite representing itself to Medicare as a retail pharmacy. FSP contracted with Fawn Lickteig’s company, Pharmacy Consulting, to complete and submit its applications to Medicare and other health care related government entities. As part of the scheme, FSP acquired information from telemedicine companies, including names and addresses of patients. FSP employees then filled and shipped medications to these people even though the doctors who wrote the prescriptions had not physically examined or conducted proper telemedicine visits with the patients. FSP received calls from patients unexpectedly receiving medical products, and some patients returned the products to FSP. FSP prioritized the filling of prescriptions based on the amount of profit Medicare would ultimately pay the pharmacy. The majority of the medications prescribed were high-dollar dermatological products. Although FSP was based in Kansas, most of the beneficiaries were Floridians, with 948 claims for Florida residents and 381 claims for Kansas residents. Of the 40 prescribing physicians who worked with FSP, 15 were under investigation at the time for referring medically unnecessary services. Between September 2020 and February 2021, Churchill, Solomon, and Lickteig submitted 2,699 false claims causing Medicare to make fraudulent payments to FSP totaling $897,405. “Medicare exists to help senior citizens obtain the medical services and supplies they need,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “Those who pillage government programs for their own enrichment will pay a heavy price when brought to justice. The agency Inspectors General under this administration are hard at work rooting out this type of fraud, and the Department of Justice stands ready to prosecute when it is found.” The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (OIG) investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sara Walton and Lindsey Debenham prosecuted the case. ### Updated October 16, 2026 Topics Benefit Fraud Healthcare Fraud Component USAO - Kansas

title: Lincoln Man Sentenced for Conspiracy to Distribute Methamphetamine
body: Press Release Lincoln Man Sentenced for Conspiracy to Distribute Methamphetamine Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nebraska United States Attorney Lesley A. Woods announced that Jessie Feaster, Jr., 50, of Lincoln, Nebraska, was sentenced on October 15, 2026, in federal court in Lincoln for conspiracy to distribute/possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine mixture and 50 grams or more of methamphetamine actual. United States District Judge Susan M. Bazis sentenced Feaster to 130 months’ imprisonment. There is no parole in the federal system. After Feaster’s release from prison, he will begin a 5-year term of supervised release. On October 10, 2025, investigators with the Lincoln Lancaster County Narcotics Task Force were conducting surveillance on co-defendant David Leibbrandt’s Lincoln residence.  They saw a U.S. Postal Service truck arrive and the driver left a package on the porch.  A short time later, someone came out of the house and retrieved the package.  About an hour later, Feaster, Jr. (“Feaster”) arrived at Leibbrandt’s residence and went inside.  After a few minutes, Feaster returned to his vehicle and left. Investigators followed Feaster to another location in Lincoln where Feaster was contacted and he agreed to let them search his car.  A sandwich bag was found on the front passenger seat which contained approximately one pound of methamphetamine.  Purity testing at the Nebraska State Patrol Crime Lab showed at least 410 grams of actual (pure) methamphetamine. Later the same day, investigators executed a search warrant at Leibbrandt’s residence.  During that search, they found seven bags containing methamphetamine with a total weight of more than 2.7 kilograms.  Purity testing on one of the packages showed at least 1.8 kilograms of actual methamphetamine.  Leibbrandt was arrested and agreed to talk to investigators.  He admitted receiving 10 pounds of methamphetamine earlier that day and said he had already sold more than three pounds from that quantity, including the pound he sold to Feaster. Leibbrandt pleaded guilty to the same conspiracy charge and was sentenced on September 24, 2026, to 135 months’ imprisonment and a 5-year term of supervised release. This case was investigated by the Lincoln/Lancaster County Narcotics Task Force. Contact Amy Donato 402-661-3700 Updated October 16, 2026 Component USAO - Nebraska

title: Northern Nevada Man Indicted for Federal Child Sexual Abuse Material Crimes
body: Press Release Northern Nevada Man Indicted for Federal Child Sexual Abuse Material Crimes Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada RENO – A Reno resident has been arrested and made his initial appearance in federal court yesterday for allegedly distributing and possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). “There is absolutely no room for leniency when it comes to the exploitation of children,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “Our office, alongside our law enforcement partners, will use every aggressive legal avenue available to dismantle this destructive cycle and ensure that predators face the maximum severity of federal law.” “Not only did Mr. Stockinger exploit these children, he further victimized them by distributing vile images of their abuse to other predators,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Field Office. “His arrest marks the first step toward ensuring he is held fully accountable for these horrific crimes. The FBI will continue to deploy every available resource through our Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force to investigate, pursue, and bring to justice the dangerous predators who target our most vulnerable.” According to allegations in the indictment, beginning about June 5, 2026, to about June 30, 2026, Zachary Steven Stockinger distributed and possessed child sexual abuse material of children younger than 12 years old engaged in sexually explicit conduct. Stockinger is charged with one count of distribution of child pornography and one count of possession of child pornography. A trial has been scheduled for December 15, 2026, before United States District Judge Miranda M. Du. If convicted, Stockinger faces a minimum penalty of five years in prison and a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison. This case was investigated by the FBI. Assistant United States Attorney Afroza Yeasmin is prosecuting the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . ### Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Nevada

title: Lincoln Man Sentenced for Possession with Intent to Distribute Methamphetamine
body: Press Release Lincoln Man Sentenced for Possession with Intent to Distribute Methamphetamine Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nebraska United States Attorney Lesley A. Woods announced that Johnathan Klein, 31, of Lincoln, Nebraska, was sentenced on October 15, 2026, in federal court in Lincoln for possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine actual. United States District Judge Susan M. Bazis sentenced Klein to 130 months’ imprisonment. There is no parole in the federal system. After Klein’s release from prison, he will begin a 5-year term of supervised release. Law enforcement learned that Klein had been dealing methamphetamine to a person between October of 2024 and March 13, 2025, in varying amounts.  They stated they bought 1/8 ounce 10 times, an ounce 30 times, four ounces twice, and 5 ½ ounces once. On March 13, 2025, a Lincoln Police Department officer committed a traffic stop on a vehicle with Klein as a passenger.  During a search of the driver’s person, a small bag of methamphetamine was found, which resulted in a search of the vehicle. A larger bag, containing two baggies of methamphetamine, was found on the front floorboard where the co-defendant driver and Klein had been sitting.  Syringes, scales, and baggies were also found in the vehicle. The two baggies of suspected methamphetamine found on the floorboard were sent to the Nebraska State Patrol Crime Laboratory. Further testing showed one of the baggies containing 57.72 grams of methamphetamine with a purity of 99.3%, resulting in at least 54 grams of methamphetamine actual.  The second bag contained 54.73 gram of methamphetamine. No purity analysis was conducted on that bag. The case is pending against the co-defendant. This case was investigated by the Lincoln/Lancaster County Narcotics Task Force. Contact Amy Donato 402-661-3700 Updated October 16, 2026 Component USAO - Nebraska

title: Baltimore Felon Pleads Guilty to Firearm Charges
body: Press Release Baltimore Felon Pleads Guilty to Firearm Charges Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Baltimore, Maryland – A Baltimore man pled guilty in federal court to firearm-possession charges. Arsenio Hall, 37, is charged with possession of a firearm and ammunition by a prohibited person. Hall is prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition due to a prior felony conviction.  Those convictions include two for second-degree assault, including a domestically related assault, along with drug-related convictions. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the guilty plea with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Commissioner Richard Worley, Baltimore Police Department (BPD). According to court documents, on December 19, 2024, members of BPD’s SWAT Team arrived at Hall’s residence to assist Baltimore County Police Department detectives with executing an arrest warrant on Hall and a search-and-seizure warrant on his residence. These warrants were related to a November 2024 shooting in Baltimore County. During the search, officers recovered a semi-automatic rifle from a baby crib inside of Hall’s bedroom. Hall faces a maximum of 15 years in prison for possession of a firearm by a prohibited person.  U.S. District Court Judge Ellen L. Hollander set sentencing for Wednesday, Jan. 13, 2027, at 11 a.m. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. This prosecution is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) and Project Safe Home. These programs bring together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce violent crime and gun violence, and to make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. On May 26, 2021, the Department launched a violent crime reduction strategy strengthening PSN based on these core principles: fostering trust and legitimacy in our communities, supporting community-based organizations that help prevent violence from occurring in the first place, setting focused and strategic enforcement priorities, and measuring the results. Project Safe Home is an initiative under the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) through the Office on Violence Against Women (OVW) to reduce domestic violence and prevent escalation to lethal violence by targeting offenders who use or possess handguns with a history of Domestic Violence. In response, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Maryland is working closely with its federal, local, and state partners — along with Baltimore City community organizations — to reduce violent crime and enhance public safety.  This partnership and coordination between the U.S. Attorney’s Office and the City of Baltimore ensures that federal resources are leveraged effectively to address intimidate-partner firearm violence. U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and BPD for their collaborative efforts in this investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Kathleen Godwin who prosecuted this case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Maryland
