title: Brazilian Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Managerial Role in Conspiracy to Launder Tens of Millions of Dollars in Illicit Cash Proceeds
body: Press Release Brazilian Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Managerial Role in Conspiracy to Launder Tens of Millions of Dollars in Illicit Cash Proceeds Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Sixth Defendant Sentenced in $30 Million Multi-State Laundering Scheme Ygor Fokin Saviolli, 35, a Brazilian national, was sentenced today to 12 years in prison for his role as a manager and supervisor in a money laundering organization that laundered more than $30 million in illicit proceeds, including the proceeds of drug trafficking. On September 24, five co-defendants received sentences ranging from 94 months in prison to 12 months and one day in prison. Gabriel Cezar Menezes, 29, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 94 months; Omar Aliperti De Mello Correa, 34, a U.S. citizen, was sentenced to 30 months; Leandro De Avila Goncalves, 43, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 24 months; and Joao Andrade De Mello, 29, and Tadeu Sebastiane Rabelo Alves Barbosa, 30, both Brazilian nationals, were each sentenced to 12 months and one day. The Brazilian national defendants were illegally residing in the United States at the time of their arrests. According to court documents, Saviolli, Menezes, Correa, Goncalves, De Mello, and Barbosa were part of a sophisticated money laundering organization that operated across the United States and spanned several countries. Members of the conspiracy arranged for U.S.-based couriers to receive bulk cash proceeds from the sale of controlled substances and then to deposit the cash at banks across the country in order to conceal and return those profits to, among others, the sources of drug supply operating outside the United States. Dozens of pickups across the country were coordinated through WhatsApp message chains that included facilitators and couriers. Saviolli provided upfront funds to facilitate the operations of the money laundering organization and oversaw the receipt and laundering of the bulk cash drug proceeds. Menezes also served as a facilitator, providing direction to and oversight of couriers, and personally picked up bulk cash on multiple occasions. Correa, De Mello, Barbosa, and Goncalves all served as couriers for the money laundering organization, conducting bulk cash pickups in cities including Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, Cleveland, Minneapolis, Rochester, and Tampa, among others. Over the course of the conspiracy, the organization concealed more than $30 million in cash. In June 2026, the defendants’ guilty pleas to conspiracy to commit money laundering were accepted by the district court. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida, and Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement. The FBI investigated the case, with assistance from the Drug Enforcement Administration’s Rochester Resident Office and Homeland Security Investigations’ Brasilia Attaché Office and Miami Field Office. Trial Attorneys James Hepburn and Jessee Alexander-Hoeppner of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Monique Botero for the Southern District of Florida prosecuted the case. MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations. MNF’s International Unit investigates and prosecutes cross-border money laundering schemes involving transnational criminal organizations, cartels, foreign official corruption and related money laundering affecting the U.S. financial system and prosecutes criminal cases and civil forfeiture matters to recover the proceeds of those crimes. Updated October 16, 2026 Components Criminal Division Criminal - Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Florida, Southern Press Release Number: 26-1217

body: Press Release Floridian sentenced to federal prison, ordered to pay $2.8M in restitution for money laundering scheme in the Eastern District of Texas Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Texas PLANO, Texas – A Palm Bay, Florida man has been sentenced to federal prison for a money laundering scheme in the Eastern District of Texas, announced U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs. Joshua Thomas Jackson, 41, pleaded guilty to money laundering and was sentenced to 51 months in federal prison by U.S. District Judge Sean D. Jordan on October 15, 2026. According to information presented in court, Jackson engaged in a scheme to defraud individuals using false representations and statements.  To facilitate the scheme, Jackson created business entities and marketed opportunities to invest in real estate development, purchases, and rehabilitation schemes. As Jackson carried out his scheme, he falsely represented that funds investors provided would be used to purchase real property or distressed residential properties, that the investors funds were secure and would be repaid within a defined period of time, and that his business activities and the victims’ investments were secure and profitable. During the period of his scheme Jackson received over $3 million from investors and caused losses to investors exceeding $2.8 million. “Investor fraud is a destructive crime and causes significant losses across our nation,” said U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs. “Together, with our partners at the FBI, we will continue to investigate and prosecute this type of fraud in the Eastern District of Texas, bring justice to these perpetrators, and seek restitution for victims.” This case was investigated by the FBI and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys in the Plano office. ### Updated October 16, 2026 Topics Fraud Financial Fraud Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Eastern

title: Leader of Lubbock Bandidos Motorcycle Club sentenced to federal prison for meth distribution
body: Press Release Leader of Lubbock Bandidos Motorcycle Club sentenced to federal prison for meth distribution Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas LUBBOCK, Texas – United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould today announced that a Lubbock man who led a high-purity methamphetamine trafficking operation was sentenced to more than 11 years in federal prison. Steven Glenn Ryals, 72, also known as “Hot Tub,” was convicted of possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine. U.S. District Judge James Wesley Hendrix imposed the 135-month sentence today. “Steven Ryals exploited his leadership of the Bandidos’ Lubbock chapter to push high purity methamphetamine into our community,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Today’s sentence sends a clear message: we will aggressively pursue those who traffic dangerous drugs and dismantle the drug distribution networks that threaten West Texans.” “Today’s sentence reflects the FBI’s continued commitment to protecting our communities from the dangers of high purity narcotics and the criminal networks that distribute them,” said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock. “This case underscores the impact of strong partnerships among federal, state, and local agencies and our shared resolve to disrupt drug trafficking organizations and hold traffickers accountable.” According to court documents, Ryals was the President of the Bandidos Motorcycle Club’s Lubbock Notorious Chapter and had served with the club for over 50 years. Federal law enforcement began investigating Ryals and other members in early 2025 for distributing methamphetamine in the Lubbock area. On Feb. 27, FBI agents and the Lubbock Anti-Gang Center executed a search warrant at the Bandidos clubhouse, which also served as Ryals’s residence. During that search, agents discovered approximately 3.2 pounds of suspected methamphetamine inside a locked filing‑cabinet drawer, along with Bandidos paraphernalia and tools used to package and distribute narcotics. At sentencing, prosecutors outlined the results of DEA laboratory testing confirming the substance was 1,449.6 grams of methamphetamine hydrochloride at 98% purity, an amount consistent only with high‑level distribution. Additional methamphetamine was found in Ryals’s bedroom closet and in his vehicle during a traffic stop on the same day, all of which he admitted possessing with intent to distribute. Ryals was previously convicted of methamphetamine trafficking and in 1999 received an identical 135‑month sentence for that offense. The FBI, the Lubbock Texas Anti‑Gang (TAG) Center and the Caprock High‑Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) conducted the investigation. TAG Center includes agents from DEA, ATF, Texas DPS, the Lubbock County Sheriff’s Office, and the Lubbock Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephen J. Rancourt prosecuted the case. ### Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Convicted Drug Dealer Charged with Trafficking Methamphetamine While Armed with Firearm, Extended Magazine, and Drum Magazine
body: Press Release Convicted Drug Dealer Charged with Trafficking Methamphetamine While Armed with Firearm, Extended Magazine, and Drum Magazine Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Hawaii HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Shalom Tuimalealiifano, 44, of Honolulu, Hawaii, was indicted on October 15, 2026 with possessing with intent to distribute methamphetamine, possession of a firearm in furtherance of drug trafficking, and unlawful possession of ammunition as a convicted felon. According to court records, Tuimalealiifano possessed methamphetamine with the intent to distribute it to others, as well as a loaded pistol with a 31-round extended magazine, which he used in furtherance of his drug trafficking.  Tuimalealiifano, who has a prior felony conviction for drug trafficking, was also charged with unlawfully possessing ammunition, including 39 rounds in a separate drum magazine. If convicted, Tuimalealiifano faces at least 20 years and up to life in prison, a fine of up to $20,000,000, plus a term of supervised release. The charges in the indictment are merely accusations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.  In the case of conviction, any sentence would be imposed by a United States District Judge based on the statutory sentencing factors and the advisory United States Sentencing Guidelines. The FBI is investigating the case. Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Heidi Turner is prosecuting the case. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe.  Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges.  As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe.  PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies.  These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Force, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. title: Banknote imagery advisory group minutes – 15 July 2026
body:
Banknote imagery advisory group minutes – 15 July 2026 | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Banknote imagery advisory group minutes – 15 July 2026 Meeting held 15 July 2026 Published on  
        16 October 2026 Date: 15 July 2026 Time: 3pm – 4pm | Location: Bank of England, Threadneedle Street, London, EC2R 8AH and MS teams Minutes Item 1 – Welcome The Chair opened the meeting by welcoming Members and outlined the purpose of the meeting. Namely, to consider the results of the 2026 banknote imagery consultation in light of the Bank’s objectives to support counterfeit resilience, and to consider which four animals to recommend to the Governor to feature as the central imagery on the next series of banknotes. The Chair reminded Members of the Bank’s obligations under the Public Sector Equality Duty throughout the imagery selection process. Item 2 – Terms of Reference Decision: Members agreed to sign off the updated Terms of Reference adding the Banknote Innovation Programme Director as a new Core Member. Item 3 – Background Members were reminded of the key milestones in the imagery selection process, including the recent consultation asking for the UK public’s views on a shortlist of animals which could feature as the central imagery on the next series of banknotes. Respondents were able to choose up to two animals from each of three different categories: Mammals; Birds; and Amphibians, Insects and Fish. Members discussed the response to the public consultation, which received nearly 500,000 responses via an online survey, post, emails and phone calls. Members were pleased with the level of public engagement and suggested it showed that the theme resonated with the public. Item 4 – Choosing which animals should feature on Series H banknotes Members were asked to consider the Bank’s objectives that the chosen imagery supports counterfeit resilience, reflects public preference and celebrates the breadth of UK nature. Members were encouraged to consider the four proposed animals as a set to ensure they are sufficiently varied in their forms, movements and habitats to maximise differentiation between each denomination, thereby aiding counterfeit resilience. Members considered the results of the June 2026 public consultation and agreed on the importance of reflecting the public’s views on banknote design alongside the Bank’s wider objectives to ensure secure and resilient banknote design. Members discussed the proposal to feature the Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee, and European hedgehog as the central imagery on the next series of banknotes. The Atlantic puffin would bring a marine environment that would not be possible with the fox or kingfisher, which had received more selections in their respective categories. This set would include the most popular animal from each of the three categories as well as the most popular marine animal in the shortlist. Members considered how each of the proposed animals’ forms and habitats could be differentiated to help the public easily identify each denomination, as well as how the proposed animals’ movements could be incorporated into security features to support authentication. It may also be possible to include some of the other animals from the shortlist as secondary imagery in the final designs. This would be subject to further engagement with the members of the Banknote Imagery Expert Panel about the animals’ habitats and note design decisions later in the process. Members concluded that the proposed set of animals met the Bank’s objectives for counterfeit resilience and took into account the outcome of the public consultation. Decision: BIAG agreed to recommend the buff-tailed bumblebee, barn owl, European hedgehog and Atlantic puffin to the Governor as the central imagery for the four denominations of Series H. Action: The Chief Cashier will send BIAG’s recommendation to the Governor for his indicative views ahead of engaging with the Expert Panel. Item 5 – Next steps Members were informed of the next steps, which includes sharing BIAG’s recommendation with the Governor and further engagement with the Expert Panel to seek their views on how the chosen animals should be depicted, including the choice of habitats to use to support differentiation. The final decision would be made by the Governor. The Bank will seek to announce the four animals to the public in the Autumn. title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
body: October 15, 2026 Research Product Bringing GPT‑Rosalind to academic research labs Introducing the Rosalind Academic Plan, offering eligible labs sponsored access to GPT‑Rosalind and tools for life sciences discovery. Apply for access (opens in a new window) Loading… Share We’re introducing the Rosalind Academic Plan to help more academic scientists access GPT‑Rosalind ⁠ , our dedicated life sciences model, which combines frontier reasoning with Rosalind workbench ⁠ (opens in a new window) that enables specialized tool orchestration across medicinal chemistry, genomics, wet-lab assistance, and other scientific applications. Eligible labs can receive up to 30 Business Standard seats at no cost for up to 12 months, with access to GPT‑Rosalind subject to trusted-access approval. Academic research creates knowledge that entire fields build on. Work that begins with a fundamental question about biology can eventually change how we diagnose disease, develop medicines, or grow food. But those advances depend on scientists having the resources to explore ideas, test them, and share what they learn. Accelerating scientific discovery is central to OpenAI’s mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. With this plan, we’re investing in the scientists doing that foundational work—helping more labs combine their expertise and judgment with AI tools built for life sciences research. Supporting the research behind future breakthroughs Many of the advances we rely on today grew out of years of basic research. The Human Genome Project helped launch modern genomics, transforming medicine, diagnostics, and biotechnology. Curiosity-driven work on bacterial immune systems led to CRISPR-Cas9, which revolutionized genome editing and is now advancing research in cancer, inherited disease, agriculture, and biotechnology. Decades of university research on mRNA also laid the groundwork for COVID-19 vaccines and a new generation of vaccines and therapies. Academic research has always laid the groundwork for advances in medicine and biotechnology. By helping more scientists combine their scientific expertise and judgment with the advanced specialized reasoning of GPT‑Rosalind, we hope to support discoveries whose benefits reach far beyond the lab. How academic labs are using GPT‑Rosalind OpenAI is committed to enabling academic researchers to pursue their scientific ambitions. Distinguished academic labs are already exploring how GPT‑Rosalind can support work ranging from protein design to understanding neurodegeneration. These examples show where researchers are applying the model within their scientific workflows. 1 of 3 “ GPT‑Rosalind helped me gather drug physicochemical parameters faster. PubChem and NCBI tools helped me work across ten drugs while refining the distinction between predicted and experimentally measured values ” Zhao Lab, UCSF “ I use GPT models throughout my research, from exploring the literature to refining experiments and computational approaches. They help me iterate on ideas much faster and explore more possibilities than ever before. I feel more efficient as a researcher, with more room to explore and think creatively. ” Dr. Mathieu Bourdenx, Bourdenx Lab “ Rosalind will not only help us improve our current discovery and design tasks, but also apply them at larger scales than previously possible while still providing useful insights to biological researchers. ” Dr. Brian Hie, Stanford University and Arc Institute Zhao Lab, UCSF Dr. Mathieu Bourdenx, Bourdenx Lab Dr. Brian Hie, Stanford University and Arc Institute Zhao Lab, UCSF Dr. Mathieu Bourdenx, Bourdenx Lab Dr. Brian Hie, Stanford University and Arc Institute What the plan includes With the new Rosalind Academic Plan, academic researchers can bring GPT‑Rosalind and Rosalind Workbench to their lab with greater flexibility and harness frontier model intelligence for scientific research. Eligible labs receive: Up to 30 Business Standard seats at $0 per user per month for up to 12 months. Access to all commercially available frontier OpenAI models, subject to plan usage limits. Access to GPT‑Rosalind following trusted-access approval. Research data shared through the Rosalind Academic Plan is not used to train our models by default. Build for life sciences research GPT‑Rosalind is a specialized life sciences model designed to support deeper reasoning on complex biological questions. Through trusted access, approved researchers can use it to investigate sensitive scientific questions within safeguards designed for legitimate research. Areas of research include: Drug and protein design Designing candidate drugs, therapeutic proteins, peptides, and enzymes, and optimizing their molecular interactions, selectivity, stability, and suitability for development. Disease detection and monitoring Identifying molecular signatures of disease and developing liquid biopsies and other minimally invasive diagnostics to detect disease earlier, monitor progression, and assess treatment response. Vaccines and immune responses Designing and evaluating antibodies and vaccines against emerging viral variants, investigating host–pathogen interactions, and studying the strength and durability of protective immune responses. Genetic and RNA therapies Developing approaches to correcting genetic defects and modulating gene expression, designing RNA therapeutics, and investigating how to deliver treatments safely and effectively to intended tissues. Agriculture and animal health Investigating crop resilience, plant disease, and animal health, and applying genetic, nutritional, and biological insights to improve food production and veterinary care. Ecology and conservation Studying biodiversity, adaptation, species interactions, and environmental exposures to understand ecosystem change and inform conservation, bioremediation, and responses to climate change. Antimicrobial resistance Studying how microorganisms resist antibiotics, antivirals, and antifungals, and developing new treatments for resistant infections, biofilms, and persistent disease. 01 / 07 Card 1 of 7: Drug and protein design Apply on behalf of your lab The Rosalind Academic Plan is currently available to academic labs at U.S. universities. PIs and lab leads at universities without an OpenAI Enterprise agreement can apply on behalf of their labs through our trusted access process. Labs at universities with an existing agreement must apply through their university’s Enterprise access process. Once approved, PIs and lab leads can activate free access to GPT‑Rosalind for up to 30 named members, alongside the other OpenAI frontier models included in the plan. API access is not included at this time. Verified PIs and lab leads manage member permissions and are responsible for their lab’s approved use. Get started with GPT‑Rosalind Choose the application path for your lab or organization. Academic labs Rosalind Academic Plan For PIs and lab leads at eligible organizations without an existing Enterprise account. Apply on behalf of your lab. Apply for academic lab access (opens in a new window) Existing Enterprise accounts GPT-Rosalind access For academic users at eligible institutions with an existing OpenAI Enterprise agreement. Request access through your existing Enterprise account. Request GPT-Rosalind access (opens in a new window) GPT‑Rosalind access is subject to approval. Learn more about eligibility, application requirements, and getting started in our help center guide ⁠ (opens in a new window) . Responsible access for scientific research Before activating access, we: Verify the institution’s legitimacy and the PI or lab lead’s identity Review the lead’s professional background, institutional appointment, and authority to oversee lab access Assess the lab’s institutional affiliation, research activities, and intended use Establish clear responsibilities for the lab lead and a designated institutional safety contact Safeguards continue after activation through monitoring and enforcement. For registered high-sensitivity use cases, our safety checks account for the approved research context. When questions arise, we may follow up with researchers to clarify the work and confirm authorization. This approach is designed to detect potential misuse while accounting for legitimate research context and reducing unnecessary interruptions to authorized work. Specialized intelligence for complex scientific questions Get started We’re starting with academic labs as part of a broader effort to put useful AI tools in the hands of more scientists. By lowering the cost of access, we hope to give more researchers room to pursue ideas whose benefits could reach far beyond their own labs—from a clearer understanding of disease to better treatments and more resilient food systems. Those advances will come from scientists asking important questions and doing the work to answer them. We want to help more of them do that work. If you’re affiliated with an academic lab, learn more about the Rosalind Academic Plan and check whether you’re eligible ⁠ (opens in a new window) . 2026 Author OpenAI Keep reading View all Helping teens learn, plan, and shape the future of AI Product Oct 7, 2026 GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone Product Oct 7, 2026 Sharing AI progress in mathematics Research Oct 6, 2026

title: Bringing the magic: Google breaks open a bottleneck in quantum computing
body: Bringing the magic: Google breaks open a bottleneck in quantum computing Oct 15, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link We've shown that magic state cultivation works on Google Quantum AI hardware. Emma Rosenfeld Research Scientist, Google Quantum AI Craig Gidney Quantum Software Engineer, Google Quantum AI Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Google Quantum AI has demonstratively opened up a key bottleneck in quantum computing: we’ve shown that “magic state cultivation” works in practice on our Willow processor, reducing errors about 40x compared to without it. This breakthrough, published today in Science , is a crucial step towards scaling up quantum computing to practical use. The "magic state" bottleneck Since 2004, long before quantum computing was a practical engineering pursuit, researchers have foreseen a particularly tricky bottleneck. To achieve “universal” quantum computing and execute useful programs, you need to be able to run (and error-correct ) a specific set of quantum operations. You can do this by first creating what are called "magic states," so dubbed because they can help you create the operations you need for going beyond classical computing. But there’s a catch: creating high-quality, error-corrected magic states is incredibly resource-heavy. Some estimates have shown that up to 95% of a quantum computer’s entire capacity might need to be dedicated to making them — leaving little room for actual computing. An extra challenge is that once you use a magic state, you can’t re-use it, making magic states a scarce resource. So for 20 years, researchers have been chipping away at this cost of magic, bringing it lower and lower. How we made this breakthrough In 2024, Google Quantum AI researchers Craig Gidney, Noah Shutty, and Cody Jones harnessed an idea from the literature, refined it, and developed what we now call “magic state cultivation.” Their approach promised an especially large reduction. The idea was that cultivation would act like a filter. You would inject a noisy state into a small region on a quantum chip, and then run a series of highly coordinated measurements to check for errors and remove any flawed attempts. Craig and team showed how that would let you grow, or “cultivate,” an exceptionally pure, low-error quantum state that you could simultaneously adapt into a larger, useful encoding. On paper, it looked great. If we could make this idea actually work on our quantum hardware, it could substantially reduce the size of the quantum computer needed for practical tasks. In practice — and on par with developing many new technologies — it required a whole series of technical innovations and engineering. As just one example, when first testing the cultivation protocol, Google Quantum AI research scientist Emma Rosenfeld was seeing data that seemed to defy the laws of physics. After months of confusion, simulations, discussions with colleagues, and consistency checks, she found that it arose from an incorrect assumption in the team’s go-to measurement technique. Specifically, a particular kind of noise in the lab caused by electrical equipment drift and temperature variation was interfering with the benchmark’s validity. The solution required a pivot in both our theoretical and engineering approaches. The team added extra control to the system to reduce the impact of that noise, and invented a new benchmarking technique to solve the issue more fundamentally, by using cultivation as a tool to measure itself. With this and many more algorithmic innovations and engineering solutions, we established a new state-of-the-art in quantum metrology. On Google Quantum AI's Willow processor, our protocol achieved an extraordinary 40-fold reduction in errors relative to un-cultivated states. And we got T-states with a record logical fidelity of 99.99%. Now published in Science , this work is the first demonstration of a practical solution to one of quantum computing's most severe resource bottlenecks. It demonstrates, on real hardware, that we can efficiently create these crucial magic states. Our findings and the future We also took the first steps in demonstrating that Craig and others’ theories are compatible with our quantum computing architecture. We learned how to successfully switch between “color codes” (one newer type of quantum error correction, ideal for cultivation) and “surface codes” (another, more established method), grafting states from a distance-3 color code to a distance-5 surface code. Originally developed in the 2024 theory paper, this grafting protocol showed that in practice, purified states can survive and transfer smoothly inside our hardware. Of course, we still need to demonstrate magic state cultivation at a larger scale to make it realistic for practical quantum computing, and plenty of technical challenges remain. But this achievement takes a key theoretical idea and turns it into an experimentally demonstrated reality. It brings us one step closer to our goal at Google Quantum AI : building a useful, error-corrected quantum computer to solve otherwise unsolvable problems. Posted in:

title: Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark
body: Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark Explore a new era of local AI, join launch celebrations around the world and #ShareYourSpark. October 15, 2026 by Shreevar Rastogi 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! A new beginning for Windows PCs starts tomorrow with the launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark — one PC built for creators, gamers and AI agents. All are invited to celebrate with NVIDIA and partners at launch events around the world. Share Your Spark Every PC has a story. What was your first Windows PC, and what did it spark a love for? Join the celebration online by sharing responses with #ShareYourSpark for a chance to win an ASUS ProArt P14 RTX Spark laptop signed by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang. See the campaign and official rules . See What Reviewers Are Saying From local AI workflows to creative apps and gaming, see what reviewers are saying about RTX Spark — then experience it at a launch celebration. “The fact that NVIDIA, Microsoft and their partners have delivered such a capable, compatible and polished platform even in its first at-bat should put the rest of the PC industry on notice.” — Tom’s Hardware “I tested NVIDIA’s RTX Spark for gaming and local AI – the performance absolutely stunned me.” — TrustedReviews , UK “I’m very happy to report that performance is actually looking really good when it comes to AI, gaming and creative workflows.” — Microcenter “[RTX Spark] is a different species of computer that has arrived early. It is a statement of intent from NVIDIA about where computing is going — trading raw benchmarking crowns for the ability to carry a self-rewriting, fully autonomous, CUDA-accelerated digital brain in your backpack.” — Tom’s Guide “One of the most impressive parts of the launch is how many apps NVIDIA has worked with to ensure optimisation with the Spark technology.” — Creative Bloq Independent testing from Artificial Analysis offers an early look at the powerful local AI performance RTX Spark brings to a laptop. Join the Launch Celebrations On Friday, Oct. 16, get hands on with RTX Spark at launch events around the world. Explore demos for creating, developing and gaming, connect with fellow enthusiasts and discover what local AI can do. Times below are local. Follow each event’s entry instructions. Space is limited. San Francisco — Best Buy, 1717 Harrison Street, 10 a.m.-12 p.m . Try hands-on demos, meet iJustine and hear fireside conversations with local tech founders. Free, first-come, first-served entry; no ticket required. Event details . Berlin — Xperion at Saturn, Alexanderplatz 3, 7-10:30 p.m . Explore hands-on demos and stage programming with creators and developers. Registration required. RSVP . Taipei — Muse Garden, No. 88 Yanchang Road . Join an evening of demos, music and AI community discussions, with shopping and networking continuing until 10:15 p.m. Registration required . Beijing — JD MALL Beijing Shuangjing Store, No. 31 Guangqu Road . Check in begins at 7 p.m. Launch celebration starts at 8 p.m., followed by hands-on demos. Event concludes at 9:30 p.m. Register through WeChat. Istanbul — Vatan Bilgisayar Topkapı, Mevlana Caddesi No. 138 . Explore hands-on demos and local creator programming. Walk-in entry; no advance registration required. Seoul — COEX East Lobby, 513 Yeongdong-daero . Hands-on demos begin at 7 p.m., with gaming and AI creator programming from 8 p.m. Event concludes at 9:30 p.m. No advance registration required. title: How we're helping the world prepare for natural disasters
body: How we're helping the world prepare for natural disasters Oct 15, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Our north star is simple yet ambitious: No one should be surprised by a natural disaster. Yossi Matias VP, Google & GM, Google Research Kate Brandt Chief Sustainability Officer Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Today is International ShakeOut Day , when millions practice earthquake drills. Our Android Earthquake Alerts System turns smartphones into a global network that can warn people before shaking arrives, and it's expanding to more countries and regions. When a natural disaster strikes, early warnings and trusted information help people prepare, respond, and stay safe. Earthquakes are only one part of our crisis resilience efforts at Google. Our AI models also help people prepare for other natural disasters: Floods: Our flood forecasting technology provides up to seven days' notice for riverine floods for more than two billion people in 150 countries and up to 24 hours' notice for urban flash floods . Cyclones: WeatherNext can predict cyclones up to 15 days out. Wildfires: Near-real-time fire boundary maps are live in 34 countries, and FireSat , a global satellite constellation, is designed to detect and track fires as small as a classroom within 20 minutes once completed. In 2025 alone, Google helped connect people with crisis information more than 10 million times per day, on average. Our north star is simple yet ambitious: No one should be surprised by a natural disaster. Learn more about our progress on crisis resilience and how we are working with partners and communities around the world to better prepare for natural disasters in our new Crisis Resilience white paper . title: Android earthquake alerts now available in more than 200 regions
body: Android earthquake alerts now available in more than 200 regions Oct 15, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link We’ve sent over one billion Android earthquake alerts. Now, we’re expanding alerts to more places and adding new details, helping more people take action and stay safe. Boone Spooner Group Product Manager, Earthquake Alerts Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link A few seconds of warning when an earthquake hits can give you crucial time to take cover and protect yourself and your loved ones. To make these early warnings possible at scale, we built the Android Earthquake Alerts System — the world’s largest mobile-based earthquake detection network. Since launching in 2021, we’ve sent over one billion alerts to help people stay safe before the shaking even starts. Today, we’re expanding the system from 98 countries and regions to more than 200 — including Panama, Guatemala and many more. We’re also improving our latest “Be Ready” alert to give you more information in seconds. If an earthquake occurs in a region where alerts are active, Android users can expect to see one of three alerts: Be Aware: A straightforward alert for estimated light shaking, letting you know an earthquake has been detected nearby. Be Ready: A detailed alert for stronger shaking, alerting you to prepare to take action. Take Action: A full-screen alert for moderate to heavy shaking, giving you immediate advice on how to stay safe. We’ve built-out our Be Ready alert with new helpful guidance. In the coming months, you’ll see a map with a radius of where we’ve detected shaking, estimated earthquake magnitude, action you can take, and a button to learn more about the earthquake as information comes in. Updated "Be Ready" alert coming soon Our physical safety products are deeply important to us. While we hope they never get used, we’re grateful to be able to bring more information to more people when they need it most. Learn more about the Android Earthquake Alerts System and where it is active . 1 To see how we're helping communities around the world better prepare for earthquakes and other natural disasters, read our new Crisis Resilience white paper . title: Open From Data Center to Desktop: NVIDIA Expands Nemotron Family With Highest Efficiency Super VL and Bolt Models
body: Open From Data Center to Desktop: NVIDIA Expands Nemotron Family With Highest Efficiency Super VL and Bolt Models 5x faster, accurate and customizable Nemotron 3.5 Super VL expands NVIDIA’s open models for always-on agents, with Nemotron 3.5 Bolt bringing agentic intelligence to local NVIDIA systems. October 15, 2026 by Kari Briski 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA today released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter model that delivers the fastest task completion and highest accuracy for specialized always-on agents. Joining it are two new edge models: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, optimized to balance intelligence and speed per GB for local agentic workloads, and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, optimized for intelligence per GB for fast conversational agents. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming Oct. 23. The three open models together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware. Any organization that wants to run agents on NVIDIA infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier, without having to choose between capability and deployability. Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside Lightning and Ultra. Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: Frontier Accuracy at One-Fifth the Size Super VL, built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition , delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL delivers frontier-level intelligence in its class for high-volume agentic workflows. As the fastest open agentic model in its class — 5x faster than the next best — it helps enterprise agents complete high-volume tasks faster across workflows that span days or weeks. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index leadboard, achieves up to 5x faster throughput compared to other models in its class. Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and oversee what they build. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: Agentic Intelligence at the Edge Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX/DGX Spark, using a native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run alongside other applications. Relative to other models with a similar memory footprint, it provides a good balance of intelligence and speed: smart enough to get most jobs done, yet much faster than the smartest models. With Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, users can delegate their projects to popular local agent harnesses — from researching the web to writing to debugging code — all without sending those workloads to the cloud. It is the #1 open model in its class on PinchBench , and the #2 open model for BrowseComp . Bolt E4B 4GB is built for physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. It combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power fast local voice assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces. Adoption of Custom Super Intelligence Dozens of organizations across industries are post-training Super VL on their own data, tools, policies and workflows to push accuracy higher on the specialized tasks that define their agent deployments. Super VL is being post-trained and customized by organizations across industries. Scale AI post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and for EY’s M&A due diligence agent. AfterQuery customized the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis. AI21 and Alice post-trained the model for cybersecurity attack resilience. Mercor post-trained the model on APEX-SWE coding benchmark, for coding agents that plan, write and debug code. ModelScope enables developers to fine-tune the model through its ms-swift framework for specialized multimodal applications. Additional organizations customizing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include Ramp for financial document intelligence; Dream , sovereign AI-powered cybersecurity research and vulnerability analysis; Lila Sciences for scientific discovery and search, and R1 for medical claims analysis and revenue cycle management. TrainLoop post-trained the model with dermatology data from Nolla, which just became the first company approved for AI to write initial patient prescriptions. Software platform companies integrating Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include: Atlassian , for tasks like agentic search across apps such as Jira and Confluence. CrowdStrike , which is customizing the model for agentic blue teaming in enterprise security. Dassault Systèmes , powering engineering design and simulation. Perplexity , for search and agentic tasks in Perplexity Search and Computer. Salesforce , which is customizing Nemotron to power AI agents that digitize and automate complex government workflows in secure customer environments through Missionforce Operations. Synopsys software for semiconductor design verification interoperates with the model. What Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Actually Sees Nemotron 3.5 Super VL’s vision language strengths are targeted at what agents encounter in practice: optical character recognition, tables, charts and structured information in visual documents. It processes a web page, extracts text, reads graphs and charts, and returns insights from what it finds. The same applies to PDFs and other documents agents commonly work with. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL understands images, webpages and PDFs and acts on that understanding. Combining text and visual understanding in one model means agents don’t need to route tasks between separate systems — context carries through as work moves from document to data to decision. Open for Maximum Control, Security, and Privacy Openness and customizability reinforce each other. The model ships with open weights, open datasets and training recipes. Control runs in two directions. Organizations can run the model wherever their security and data-residency requirements dictate. They also choose to adopt a model they can adapt, rather than one subject to a provider’s restrictions. In insurance, for example, a customized agent can scan claims for fraud markers on repeat. In financial services, an agent can review credit scores and flag activity against an organization’s own lending criteria. The model stays on premises. The data stays private. Customization is supported through NVIDIA NeMo, Python-based pipelines and open datasets. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across pretraining and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments. NVIDIA is also releasing open datasets on Hugging Face spanning agentic tool use , finance, instruction following, long context, fairness and vision-language understanding, along with the reinforcement learning environments in NeMo Gym. NVIDIA NIM packages the model as a production-ready microservice with performance-optimized, validated configurations and enterprise-grade support, refreshed every two weeks with security patches and performance improvements. And with the model running on NVIDIA Dynamo, organizations can serve up to 8x more users with 85% lower latency. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available now on Hugging Face, Open Router, ModelScope community and as NVIDIA NIM. Runs on DGX Spark, DGX Station, and RTX Nemotron 3.5 Super VL runs across NVIDIA’s full hardware stack: on DGX Spark , DGX Station ,  RTX PRO and RTX systems for local intelligence at the desktop, on NVIDIA Jetson at the edge, and across data center and cloud environments. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24G B is available now on Hugging Face, with support for llama.cpp, Ollama , LM Studio , Unsloth , and vLLM . Built for NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops arriving Oct. 16, it also runs on GeForce RTX PCs , DGX Spark , DGX Station and RTX PRO workstations . Download the open weights , explore customization resources with NVIDIA NeMo, or read the technical blog for the full architecture breakdown. Stay up to date on agents, NVIDIA Nemotron and more by subscribing to NVIDIA news , joining the community , and following NVIDIA AI on LinkedIn , Instagram , X and Facebook . Explore self-paced video tutorials and livestreams . See notice regarding software product information. title: Making your Pixel devices last longer through design, repair, and reuse
body: Making your Pixel devices last longer through design, repair, and reuse Oct 15, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link This International Repair Day, here’s a look at how we design for longevity — from the modular engineering of our Pixel smartwatch to our global network of walk-in repair centers. You can now manage your device health, troubleshoot issues, or start a repair directly through the My Pixel app and our updated support hubs. Generative AI is experimental. "Making your Pixel devices last longer" explains how Google is prioritizing repair and sustainability. New Pixel watches and Fitbit trackers use modular designs to make repairs much easier. You can use the My Pixel app to troubleshoot issues or start repairs quickly. Google’s expanded trade-in and refurbished programs help keep older devices out of landfills. These efforts aim to reduce electronic waste by helping your tech last much longer. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Google is designing its new watches and trackers to be much easier to fix instead of just throwing them away. They’ve made it simple to find repair guides, get expert help, or even chat with an AI to troubleshoot problems. If you're ready for an upgrade, you can trade in your old device or buy a refurbished one to keep tech out of landfills. It’s all about making your gadgets last longer so you don't have to replace them as often. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Our devices should be built to last — and easy to repair when life happens. As we celebrate International Repair Day , we are reflecting on how circularity shapes everything we build. Extending the lifespan of hardware is one of the most meaningful ways to reduce e-waste and maximize the value of our technology. Here’s a closer look at how we are making repair and reuse more accessible, dependable, and impactful. Designing devices for repairability: The Pixel Watch & Fitbit Edge Sustainable hardware begins with thoughtful engineering. For the Pixel Watch 4 and 5, our design and engineering teams established an ambitious repairability roadmap and identified common repair bottlenecks from the earliest stages of development. The result is an industry-leading modular architecture that rejects the industry standard of heavily glued, unserviceable components. And according to iFixit, it's the most repairable smartwatch out there , earning a 9 out of 10 repairability score. And this week we expanded our repairable products with the new Fitbit Edge , our first repairable fitness tracker, featuring an internal modular architecture and a replaceable battery designed to extend the life of your device. Making it easy for you to access expert Pixel support Great design must be backed by fast, reliable support when you need it. Here are all the ways Pixel customers can extend the life of their devices. Flagship device protection: Pixel Care+ offers eligible users peace of mind with protection against cracks, spills, drops, and more. My Pixel app on-device support: The Support tab in My Pixel is a hub to find solutions. Head there to run diagnostics, chat with an AI agent to troubleshoot an issue, or easily start a repair. Google Store repair information hubs: We launched country-specific repair support pages that feature multiple repair solutions and transparent price estimates, helping you find the best option for their needs. A new, simplified repair process: Our self-service repair program is now integrated with Your Devices , so you can quickly verify your Pixel device details and start a hassle-free repair. Global walk-in repair network: Through our global network of walk-in service centers and authorized providers, you can access quick, certified repairs with genuine parts. Google Store trade-in program: When it's time for an upgrade, our Google Store Trade-In Program makes it easy to exchange eligible devices for store credit, so older devices get safely refurbished or responsibly recycled. Expanding our certified pre-owned program The Google Certified Refurbished program keeps high-performing hardware in circulation longer, without compromising on quality or performance. Every phone in the program is restored with genuine Google parts, updated with the latest Android software, packaged in 100% plastic-free materials, and backed by our full one-year warranty. To make sustainable upgrades even more accessible, we’re expanding the program on two fronts: we added the Pixel 9 series to our U.S. lineup at up to 45% off on the Google Store Online U.S ., and we launched certified refurbished devices on the Google Store Online Japan this October. We'll continue to invest in sustainability, product longevity, and repair to extend the lifespan of our products. And we invite you to join us in this journey: whether you are checking your device’s health via the My Pixel app , exploring repair options , or opting for a Certified Refurbished device. title: Dial Up the Cloud: NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Controls Arrive on GeForce NOW
body: Dial Up the Cloud: NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Controls Arrive on GeForce NOW Plus, stream ‘Enshrouded’ 1.0 and ‘Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2’ alongside 10 new games this week. October 15, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Dial in the next gaming session this GFN Thursday. New NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 controls give GeForce NOW members more choice over how supported games look and perform in the cloud, even without the latest hardware. Then, step into the Shroud as Keen Games’ Enshrouded leaves early access with its 1.0 release, or let the bolts fly in Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 . Both are streaming on GeForce NOW at launch. With 10 new games joining the cloud this week, members can put the new controls to work in supported titles and keep playing across supported devices without downloads, installs or expensive hardware upgrades. Fine-Tune the Cloud With DLSS 4.5 Controls More control, more cloud power. NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 controls are now available on GeForce NOW, giving members more choice over how supported games look and perform in the cloud, even without the latest hardware. DLSS Super Resolution sharpens image quality, while Dynamic Multi Frame Generation delivers lower latency and reduces stutter for smoother streaming, and Ray Reconstruction enhances ray-traced visuals. In addition, Ultimate members streaming on GeForce RTX 5080-powered cloud rigs benefit from the maximum available options, including Dynamic Multi Frame Generation up to 4X. From James Bond’s globe-trotting missions in 007 First Light — now with path tracing support — to CONTROL Resonant ’s reality-bending Manhattan and the shadowy scares of Resident Evil Requiem , the controls help fine-tune supported games for image quality, responsiveness or a preferred balance between the two. These new settings are available in the GeForce NOW app under settings, for Windows, macOS, Chrome OS and Steam OS platforms. Members can read here for more details on using the feature with their membership tier, and more information on how to get the smoothest cloud game streaming for some games on GeForce NOW. Rise, Flameborn Enshrouded 1.0 brings the co-op survival action role-playing game out of early access and into its full release. Rise as a Flameborn, the last ember of hope of a dying race, and venture into a vast world of survival, action and role-playing, where a corrupting fog has consumed a once-beautiful kingdom. The title brings improvements to existing systems, alongside expansions in combat with nine new spells, new mage and archer skills, reworked wands and upgradeable Eternal spells and arrows. New enemy variants keep encounters fresh, while a new biome raises the player level cap to 50 and equipment cap to 55. GeForce NOW offers Enshrouded 1.0 ready to play in the cloud at launch across supported devices. Skip the 60GB local install to save precious storage space, then step into the Shroud without waiting for downloads or needing to make room for the update. Let the Bolts Fly Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 is now streaming on GeForce NOW. The brutal, fast-paced sequel to the retro first-person shooter brings more enemies, more weapons and new ways to purge. Picking up directly after the original game, a branching single-player campaign sends the fight to grimdark new worlds. Choose between the formidable Sternguard Veteran Malum Caedo and the swift Sister of Battle Nyra Veyrath, each with distinct abilities, weapons and play styles. From towering hive cities to jungle mangrove swamps, new enemy types await in every biome. GeForce NOW keeps the campaign ready in the cloud. No local rig upgrades or game installs stand between members and the fight — the Emperor’s work waits for no loading bar. In addition, members can look for the following joining the GeForce NOW library : Deep Dish Dungeon (New release on Steam , Oct. 13) Planet Zoo 2 (New release on Steam , Oct. 13) Total War: SHOGUN 2 – Complete Edition (New release on Steam , Oct. 13) Valor Mortis (New release on Steam , Oct. 13) Among the Trolls (New release on Steam , Oct. 14) over the hill (New release on Steam , Oct. 14) Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 (New release on Steam , Oct. 14) Beyond These Stars (New release on Steam and Xbox , Oct. 15), available on Game Pass Tenebris Somnia (New release on Steam , Oct. 16) The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered ( Xbox ), available on Microsoft Store Also this week, the performance of DLSS 5’s 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model is improving by 2X, enabling even more gamers to enjoy DLSS 5’s transformative uplift in lighting and materials at high frame rates and settings. The new, more performant DLSS 5 model will debut in NBA 2K27 on Oct. 16 on GeForce NOW, GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and RTX Spark laptops. Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after they’re released and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates to announced titles. Gamers who want to test out the new 4.5 controls and high-performance GeForce NOW cloud gaming can start with a day pass to try premium cloud gaming before committing to a membership. Better yet, the cost of the day pass can be applied toward a first monthly membership — making it easy to try GeForce RTX-powered cloud gaming with the latest releases, then level up for more. What’s on the playlist this weekend? Let us know on X or in the comments below. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer As we build for the future of commerce, our focus spans two fronts: unlocking agentic capabilities that act on your behalf, and designing practical tools that give shoppers confidence and control. Google’s Universal Cart is built for that second track — mirroring how people actually shop today across Google, without losing track of their items, their savings, or the merchants they trust. The Universal Cart , which we previewed earlier this year, is an intelligent shopping cart and your new hub for shopping on Google. The cart puts you in control, helping to organize your shopping, keep track of items you love from across retailers, stay on top of promos, and enjoy effortless checkout powered by the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP). Today, Universal Cart is rolling out in the U.S. across Google Search and in the Gemini app. The cart for all your shopping Here are four things the new Universal Cart lets you do to stay organized and shop more confidently this holiday season. 1. Save products from multiple retailers, wherever you’re shopping on Google. Universal Cart offers a more organized alternative to tabs and screenshots. The cart saves your progress across Google so you never have to start your shopping from scratch. Let’s say you save a handbag from Steve Madden to your cart in AI Mode in Search , and later a sweater from Quince and lipgloss from Ulta Beauty in the Gemini app. Those products will be there in your cart when you come back later so you can pick up right where you left off. 2. Keep tabs on pricing or inventory changes for your entire list. The cart is built on the 60+ billion continually refreshed product listings in Google’s Shopping Graph. This allows it to proactively work for you in the background, sending notifications about price drops or when an item comes back in stock. 3. Identify hidden savings or points from your cart. The cart’s intelligent reasoning can help anticipate your needs. Say you have a couple different credit cards, but don’t know each one’s specific benefits. The Universal Cart is built on Google Wallet so it understands your card perks and can intelligently help you choose between payment methods. It’ll also show you relevant promo codes right from the cart. 4. Make seamless, trusted purchases when you’re ready to buy. In online shopping, trust is everything. You can securely check out with Google Pay in just a few taps with many of your favorite stores right in the cart, or you can transfer your items directly to the merchant’s cart to finish buying on their site. Try these simplified checkout experiences with merchants like Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair, and many Shopify merchants. Either way, you will receive direct confirmations and customer support from the merchant, and they will remain the seller of record. As the holiday season kicks into high gear, the Universal Cart is just one way we’re giving shoppers the convenience and smarts they need to make the best shopping choices. title: Teaching students to think and learn through questions
body: October 15, 2026 Company Teaching students to think and learn through questions Loading… Share On Teachers’ Day, we celebrate those who help us learn. A good question can change the course of a lesson. It can bring an unspoken question to light, open up another way to solve a problem, or help someone recognize what they already know. Teachers do this work every day: they know their students, choose how to introduce an idea, and guide them from their first attempt to understanding. Set in a university classroom, the campaign takes a humorous look at the changing relationship between teachers and students and celebrates the role of educators in a world with AI. AI for Educators now available in Portuguese Today, we are launching the AI for Educators ⁠ (opens in a new window) course in Brazilian Portuguese on OpenAI Academy, OpenAI’s free learning platform. Designed for educators in primary, secondary, and higher education, the course shows how to use AI to plan lessons, create activities and assessments, and prepare communications while preserving educators’ pedagogical judgment. Learning through active participation, step by step Study Mode helps you explore a subject ⁠ (opens in a new window) step by step, with questions, hints, explanations, and checks for understanding. Developed in collaboration with teachers, scientists, and experts in pedagogy, the feature aims to encourage active participation and reflection on one’s own reasoning. To turn on Study Mode , select Study from the tools menu in ChatGPT. A student reviewing biology, for example, might ask: “I’m studying enzymes. Ask me one question at a time, wait for my answer, and help me identify what I need to review.” Teachers can also try Study Mode with subjects they know well, looking at whether the questions encourage reasoning and whether the explanations are appropriate for their class. In a science lesson on evaporation, for example, a teacher might ask students to investigate why clothes dry on a clothesline. After exploring the topic with Study Mode, each student writes their own explanation and a question to discuss in class, without referring back to the conversation. The teacher can use these responses to identify what needs to be revisited with the class. This Teachers’ Day, we invite you to experiment: explore the AI for Educators course, try Study Mode, and discover how these tools can be useful in different teaching contexts. Technology can open up new ways to learn, but it is teachers who know their students, ask the most important questions, and help turn curiosity into knowledge. 2026 ChatGPT Education Author OpenAI Keep reading View all Atlassian and OpenAI expand their partnership Company Oct 6, 2026 How Albertsons Companies is reimagining retail from the inside out Company Oct 1, 2026 DevDay 2026 Recap Company Sep 29, 2026

title: TIME has named Google SynthID one of the Best Inventions of 2026.
body: TIME has named Google SynthID one of the Best Inventions of 2026. Oct 15, 2026 TIME has named Google SynthID to its annual list of Best Inventions . As generative AI makes digital media more realistic, knowing how content was made helps you navigate the web with confidence. Google SynthID embeds an invisible, durable digital watermark into AI-generated images, audio, video, and text at the moment of creation, without altering the quality. To date, SynthID has watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio. We also recently announced SynthID Bio , bringing SynthID’s watermarking technology to synthetic biology. To help people identify AI content, verification tools are built directly into Google Search, the Gemini app, and Chrome. You can also use the SynthID Detector to check content from Google and our partners. Together, these tools help give you more transparency and context around the content you encounter online. You can read more about this and other inventions on TIME’s website .

Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Finding the perfect holiday gift shouldn't feel like a guessing game. To take the stress out of your shopping, we analyzed historical promotional patterns, Search trends, and discount data across U.S. merchants on Google. The result is our When to Buy Guide , a research-backed roadmap showing when holiday discounts may hit their peak, based on data from last year. Here are a few tips and findings to help you shop smarter. For the full list of pricing trends and insights into our last-minute gifting habits, read the complete When to Buy Guide . You'll also discover which parent we shop for later, and which state claims the most last-minute shoppers. Snag your scent before the holiday rush: If you're eyeing a perfume or cologne for someone on your list, shop early. Fragrance discounts don’t typically increase as Christmas approaches, and the volume of fragrance deals drops off sharply, so waiting until late December may not offer lower prices — and could leave you with fewer options. Strategize by buying fragrances within the first two weeks after Black Friday weekend for the best deals and inventory selection. Reconsider the Black Friday handbag frenzy: If you’re on the lookout for the perfect handbag at the best price, consider holding off on buying during Black Friday weekend. Target mid-December to balance a high discount with a decent selection of styles, or wait until late December if you just want the lowest price on remaining inventory. Shop early for travel accessories, but later for suitcases: While travel accessories see their best deals in November, major items, such as large luggage and suitcases, don't typically hit their deepest markdowns until clearance sales in late December. With this in mind, consider buying travel accessories and packing cubes on Black Friday, but wait until late December for deep clearance discounts on large suitcases, though there may be less selection. Want a tech toy deal? Wait for it: Unlike traditional electronics, categories like motorized tech toys show some of their steepest markdowns emerging in the final weeks of December. If electronic toys are on your kids’ wish lists, consider holding out until the final shopping stretch to unlock surprise last-minute savings. If you wait to buy, keep an eye on holiday shipping deadlines, unless you plan on shopping in-store. title: NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute
body: NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute NVIDIA’s participation in the European Commission’s AI in Science Enablers Initiative deepens its commitment to supporting the pursuit of scientific progress across the region. October 15, 2026 by Rod Evans 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Much of today’s scientific progress begins with computation. But turning accelerated computing’s potential into scientific progress — modeling climate systems, designing molecules, simulating materials and more — depends on more than breakthrough technology. Especially for smaller labs, early-career scientists or science-based startups, the hardest part of research can be everything that comes before the science: assembling tools, finding compute and building the expertise to use both. At the AI in Science Summit in Dublin today, the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative, a shared framework connected to RAISE — the Resource for AI Science in Europe — that brings private-sector support closer to Europe’s research community. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements NVIDIA is joining the campaign , providing: Access to accelerated tools, models and platforms Compute, cloud resources, data and scientific resources Skills, training and technical support Collaborative projects and pilots along with support for researchers and talent Support for startups and ecosystem development “Europe’s ambition in AI in science can only become reality if we bring together the strengths of our research community, industry and other partners,” Ekaterina Zaharieva, European Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation. “Through the AI in Science Enablers campaign, we are turning this ambition into concrete commitments that give researchers access to the tools, expertise and resources they need to innovate.” Open Models NVIDIA’s pledge begins with open source technology. NVIDIA has released more than 250 open models, 250 open datasets and over 1,400 open source software projects spanning large language models, healthcare, robotics, climate science, physical AI, autonomous vehicles and scientific research. The models and datasets are available on Hugging Face and GitHub. Building on this open ecosystem, researchers can build agentic reasoning capabilities with NVIDIA Nemotron — a family of architectures, open weights, open source models, training data and recipes — and scientific software including NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit , NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo libraries, NVIDIA Earth-2 models and NVIDIA ALCHEMI NIM microservices to accelerate research across biology, chemistry, molecular design, weather and climate, energy, engineering, physics and material sciences. Skills and Training Building advanced intelligence capability across Europe requires knowledge that travels as freely as compute. The NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute has launched a new open source courseware hub with hands-on course materials covering accelerated computing and deep learning — freely downloadable and openly licensed, with no enrollment, fees or deadline. Modular by design, the courses can be adapted for university curricula, supercomputing center bootcamps or developer community events, and serve as a direct bridge to NVIDIA’s broader training and certification programs . Access to Compute NVIDIA is collaborating with cloud infrastructure partners and European national AI factories — including in France , Spain and Sweden — to open new routes for startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to access sovereign European compute and services. The NVIDIA Inception program for startups provides access to compute resources and technical support, lowering the barrier to entry for startups seeking high-performance infrastructure and technological education. AI2F in France is the first AI factory to have collaborated with the Inception program for four months, demonstrating strong results. The BSC AI Factory ran a pilot initiative and is now rolling out its first full accelerator program, with growing interest from other European national AI factories in replicating the model in 2027. Beyond startup support, this program is designed to contribute to a broader strategic objective: building self-sustaining AI ventures in Spain and Europe. Sweden AI Factory , one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories, announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and SMEs enterprises across sectors including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming. Finally, EuroHPC supercomputing centers such as CINECA and JSC provide academia and startups with free access to NVIDIA GPU infrastructure and services for open research. NVIDIA complements this access with office hours, bootcamps and hackathons that help researchers fine-tune models on their own datasets. As an example, NVIDIA is co-organizing an European AI hackathon this month alongside Austrian Scientific Computing , the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre , the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart and The Cyprus Institute, for Pharos-CY . AI Infrastructure Expansion To top it all off, NVIDIA is powering Europe’s most ambitious expansion of AI infrastructure to date, with 35 supercomputers currently in development across the continent — the largest single-year buildout of supercomputing capacity Europe has ever seen. Together, these systems will equip over 3 million researchers with next-generation infrastructure, accelerating discovery across domains from climate science and drug development to materials research and beyond. Explore NVIDIA technologies for science and open source courseware , and find hands-on training through the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute . Follow the European Commission’s RAISE Pledging Initiative .
